At the other end, Virginia Tech's ground game produces a near-negative EPA per rush, inviting SMU to put Ethan Grunkemeyer in obvious passing situations. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Steve Helwick · SB Nation Thu, November 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Time and date: Friday, November 6 at 7:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-6) Over/under: 56.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 2-1 Last meeting: SMU 28, Virginia Tech 25 — September 21, 1974 Current streak: SMU, 2 (1973-74) Setting the scene While No. 1 Miami (FL) and No. 14 Wake Forest are the only ACC teams that reside in the AP Top 25, the conference title race is far from finished. There are five two-loss teams lurking right behind, and two of them clash Friday night in Dallas. It's the first meeting between SMU and Virginia Tech as ACC opponents, however, it's a familiar head coaching matchup: Rhett Lashlee and James Franklin stood on opposite sidelines as recently as 2024 in the College Football Playoff. There's plenty on the line for the bowl eligible opponents. A win would do wonders for remaining in the ACC race, especially for SMU, which can still capture a tiebreaker against Wake Forest. But a third conference loss is essentially an elimination in a 17-team league. Virginia Tech Hokies outlook BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies greets Kaleb Spencer #3 before the game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Virginia Tech (6-2, 3-2 ACC) can make another statement on the road after its bye week. The Hokies haven't rattled off seven wins in a regular season since 2019, but that streak could end Friday in year one of the James Franklin era. Virginia Tech is fresh off its biggest win under Franklin, taking down Clemson 20-16 in Death Valley on Oct. 24. Close games have been commonplace for the Hokies this season. Each of their last six contests were decided by 10 points or fewer. Three featured lead changes in the final five minutes, while another ended on a missed field goal attempt that would have resulted in a lead change. The restoration of Virginia Tech football can be attributed to the passing game. Quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer followed Franklin from Penn State and has drastically improved in his junior campaign. Grunkemeyer has connected on an efficient 71.4 percent of attempts — seventh nationally among quarterbacks with 100 attempts — and has delivered 17 touchdowns against two interceptions. Grunkemeyer has eclipsed 300 yards three times and finished seven of his eight starts without throwing a pick. Two receivers have carried a bulk of the load. Wide receiver Que'Sean Brown ranks atop the team with 51 receptions and 685 receiving yards, and he's secured at least five receptions in all eight games. Tight end Luke Reynolds has also been a matchup nightmare for defenses. Reynolds' 50 receptions rank first and his 491 receiving yards ranks third among all FBS tight ends. While a bulk of his production occurred in September, his outing against Clemson was a productive one, snagging two touchdowns on seven receptions. The Hokies aren't as adept in the run game, where they check in at 111th in the FBS with 3.7 yards per carry. They don't incorporate much quarterbaack mobility and primarily rely on the duo of Jeffrey Overton Jr. and Marcellous Hawkins Jr. Overton, a common weapon in the receiving game, showed the extent of his powers in a 209-yard rushing explosion against Boston College. Hawkins has been a steady secondary back, and he's tied for the team lead with five rushing touchdowns. Virginia Tech only surrendered more than 26 points once this season, and that was a Friday night matchup against Pittsburgh. The Hokies' defense has been a positive for the team, tied for 35th in points allowed and ranked 27th in yards allowed per game. Their strength involves limiting the run, where they give up just 93.4 yards per game on a 3.0 average. Sacks heavily factor into that total, and Virginia Tech is the best in the ACC and the sixth-best in the nation at getting to the quarterback, producing 3.4 sacks per game. It's a defensive end led effort. Aycen Stevens ranks first in the conference with 8.0 sacks, while his fellow defensive ends Cortez Harris and Mylachi Williams have 5.0 and 4.5, respectively. The Hokies haven't been as strong on the back end, but they prevent explosive plays well. No team has recorded a 50-yard completion on this defense all season. But what Virginia Tech needs to improve upon is its turnover output. The Hokies forced just five takeaways through eight games, causing the team to enter Friday with a minus-4 in the turnover battle this season. SMU Mustangs outlook DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 17: Southern Methodist University Mustangs defensive end Marques White (16) rushes the passer during the game between SMU and Virginia on October 17, 2026 at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by George Walker/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images SMU (6-2, 4-2 ACC) dropped from the rankings after a heartbreaking 30-27 loss at Syracuse last weekend. It was only the Mustangs' fourth conference defeat since joining the ACC, and the third in which they held a lead in the final minute. However, SMU has never lost back-to-back ACC games and owns an 11-0 record in ACC play at home, giving Rhett Lashlee's team the perfect opportunity to bounce back and remain in the conference title race. Slow starts have been the Mustangs' kryptonite. In their last five ACC games, they haven't scored more than 13 points in a half or entered the break with a lead larger than three. However, they've won each of their last five second halves, finishing a plus-68 over that span. SMU's offense is led by Kevin Jennings, who is one of seven passers averaging over 300 yards per game. This season has been a masterclass in efficiency for the senior, who is completing passes at a 73.7 percent clip — the third-highest rate in the country among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. Jennings has also thrown 152 consecutive passes without an interception, with his last misfire coming in the first quarter of a Sept. 26 matchup against Missouri State. The Mustangs' receiver room is as deep as they come, with five different players over the 200-yard threshold. Yamir Knight is the leader with 44 receptions for 523 yards, while Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale can also pose as explosive threats for an offense that ranks fifth nationally in 50+ yard receptions. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrstrom are also incorporated into the passing game, and they tie for the team lead with four receptions apiece. Unlike SMU's first ACC defeat at Louisville, last Saturday's loss to Syracuse was largely determined in the trenches. The Mustangs uncharacteristically allowed six sacks, accounting for 43 percent of their season total. Additionally, they struggled to create space for the running backs, which never broke off an explosive gain. Kendrick Raphael has posted three 100-yard games already in ACC play, and he can also do damage out of the backfield as a receiving option. SMU's defense didn't necessarily have a bad outing at Syracuse, limiting the Orange to 5.9 yards per passing attempt and 3.7 yards per rush. But the Mustangs surrendered conversions on all four of Syracuse's fourth down attempts, allowing the Orange to sustain otherwise lost drives. A veteran defensive line full of super seniors is the strength of the unit. SMU ranks 15th nationally with 2.9 sacks per game, and eighth-year senior Marques White leads the way with 5.5 sacks, while the rest of the sacks are quite evenly distributed. The pressure goes hand-in-hand with a strong passing defense, and SMU ranks 28th nationally in fewest passing yards allowed at 182 per game. That is the most improved element of the Mustangs from last year, but losing starting strong safety Tyren Polley for the year could make things difficult down the road. Sael Reyes stepped up last game with 10 tackles in his second start of the season, while Jimmy Wyrick recorded eight from the other safety spot. Lastly, turnovers have been a significant determinant in SMU results this season. The Mustangs lost the turnover battle 5-0 in their two losses, and they're the only bowl eligible team at a minus-5 or worse this season. These 6-2 teams are structured somewhat similarly: strong passing attacks with tight end utilization, dominant defensive fronts that repeatedly get to the quarterback, and solid defenses hampered by poor turnover margins. Short weeks oftentimes favor the home team, and SMU remains perfect against ACC opponents at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Given SMU's discrepancy between first and second half performance, Virginia Tech may enter halftime with the lead, but the Mustangs ultimately rally behind Kevin Jennings in the fourth quarter to secure a one-score win on The Hilltop. Prediction: SMU 30, Virginia Tech 24

picks.blurb: Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Virginia Tech Hokies vs. SMU Mustangs: News, Information, and Predictions Stike up the Hokie Pokey, Tech Triumph, and the Victory Tag. | John Schneider - SB Nation John Schneider · SB Nation Fri, November 6, 2026 at 4:59 AM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a short week after a week break. The Hokies are heading to Dallas to face off against the Southern Methodist University Mustangs. The Hokies are up against another major ACC opponent, and winning the game means advancing in the ACC and potentially seeing a ranking. Crossover Week Mayhem Just a note from us: Well, the first week in November through the first week of December is always a challenge for coverage. The soccer teams are wrapping up with decent enough records, but their seasons aren't quite over. The Women's Basketball Team has opened their home record at 2-0, and the Men's team also graced Cassell with a W. All of that puts a real strain on coverage so bear with us as we sort out schedules, and fight fall health issues and work vs. Hokie sports balance. The football team isn't finished, though. There are still four games left on the schedule, and then we get to plan on bowl coverage this season. Isn't that a happy event? The Hokies are bowl eligible just a couple of games after the halfway point, and that's a very pleasant occurrence. To think that we are actually paying attention to the bowl invitation list, instead of worrying on Thanksgiving weekend whether or not a win will net an invitation somewhere. The first thing to cover is a bit of fun. The ACC Network desk hosts Eric McClain and Eddie Royal had a bet going. Remember, McClain is a former Clemson player, and we all know and love Eddie Royal. So, the bet was that the loser had to wear the winner's mascot costume. Eddie was not dressed as a Tiger with the googly eyes for the TV segment. ( Congratulations to the Virginia Tech Cheer Squad equipment folks and Travis Wells for getting most of an actual Hokie Bird big enough for Eric. ) The Virginia Tech Wrestling Team received a massive boost from a wrestler who hasn't even wrestled his first match as a Hokie, yet, but who is already a world champion. Freshman Bo Bassett traveled to Kazakhstan and netted the program its first world championship and was the first American in 20 years to win in his weight class (65KG – for those lacking metric conversion skills that's 143 pounds ). The Coach Robie is going to have an absolutely dominant wrestling team this season. Back to Football Stuff It looks like the team is going to be wearing head to toe all-whites for this one. Go get your coffee, or a quick snack and listen in on Coach Franklin's weekly presser. As Bryan posted up earlier, this time the Hokies have some really good news coming out of the locker room as it pertains to the Offensive Line. Montavious Cunningham and Brody Meadows are back up to speed and are expected to play on Friday night. The O-Line has been dipping into the #3s on the depth chart for the past few games, and getting them back is a serious update to the struggling run game. That All Leads to This… Predictions The SMU Mustangs are largely a Big XII import with a near automatic bubble to the top of the ACC football pile. It's Dallas, TX, and football is a near religion for Texas. That means the program is well funded, with premium coaching, and players doused liberally with NIL funding. Up until last weekend, the Mustangs were sporting a very respectable one loss record. Until they showed up in the Syracuse (whatever they call the Carrier Dome, now), as expected in the beginning of the season SMU was challenging hard for the #2 bid in the ACC fake Championship game ( until the conference goes back to divisions and division champs who play everyone else in the division the game in Charlotte will remain fake to me ). Then the Mustangs got treated to the old Big East upset win by the Orange. That knocked them down a peg but also put the Hokies in the position of earning the #3 spot on the ACC leader board. That all means that this game might not mean an ACC bid, but it will mean a much better bowl game situation over the holidays. Bowls mean big broadcast money, and the program needs the cash to make up for a restricted gate at Lane. The Mustangs are favored by slightly less than a touchdown for this one, in their house no less. We'll see how we feel about that. This is a big test for the Hokies. Virginia Tech had a huge win at Clemson two weeks ago. No, this isn't the same Clemson team as only a few years ago, but it means something for other ACC teams to walk into Death Valley and win. SMU is better than the Tigers, but they aren't unbeatable. The clear difference here is the quarterback position. SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings is a stud. He also has one of the ACC's best running backs and one of the top receiving units in the league. This is a huge challenge for VT defensive coordinator Brent Pry. Offensively, I think the Hokies have success moving the ball. SMU's size on the defensive interior concerns me, especially with Tech's OL struggles. There is hope that with Cunningham and Meadows back, the offensive line is better, but we'll see. I expect a close game. My heart says the Hokies, my head says SMU in a close one. SMU 34, Hokies 31 This game all depends on how the Mustangs adjusted to their Syracuse loss, and if the Hokies on both sides of the ball can adjust to how the Orange controlled the SMU offense, and how they managed to get by their defense. SMU, interestingly enough, has a similar offensive/defensive balance to Tech's than we have seen this season. There are lots of "IFs" in this game, and the biggest one is "IF" the Tech defense can limit the SMU offense to what it's been scoring over the season against peer teams, the Hokies have a much better chance to win than the listed 6-point betting gimme to SMU. The latest projected O/U is 56.5, which tells me volumes of information. The analysts see this as a very close game, and the end result being less than a full score between the two teams. If the Hokies stay away from getting enamored of the run game and go downfield fast and consistently in the air on quick developing intermediate routes to their best receivers, there will be run opportunities. If Tech decides to try to "establish the run" the offense could bog down into chronic 3-and-outs. The return of two key #1/#2 depth chart players is not an excuse to try to revert to 1960's caveman Johnny Unitas two runs and a pass offense. If the Hokies move the ball and do it fast, they have enough defense ( which needs to put serious pressure on the quarterback on every play ) to hold the Mustangs to a 3.5 score effort. The Hokies are capable of 4 or more. That's a whole lot of "Ifs" though. Here's the skinny… the first team to score over 30 points wins. That puts my prediction hat on, and I think the Hokies might just be good for it, regardless of the conditions. Just a quick reminder of the times and broadcast information. It's an ESPN deal.

Ahead of the clash, here's our staff's predictions as to what will unfold tonight in the Lone Star State. JACKSON CAUDELL: While it will still be a long shot even if they find a way to win, the Hokies' ACC hopes are on the line tomorrow night at SMU. The Mustangs are also battling for their ACC title hopes, and that makes this a fascinating matchup. This is a chance for James Franklin to land another win against one of the better programs in the conference, and I think they have the offense to take advantage of a suspect SMU defense. If the Hokies can get after Kevin Jennings and force a few turnovers, I think they are able to do that and score a big win. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 31, SMU 27 JAMES DUNCAN: Syracuse left a blueprint last Saturday, beating SMU 30-27 on a touchdown with 17 seconds left. Virginia Tech is built to follow it. Nobody has beaten the Hokies by more than five points this season, and they come in with 13 days of rest to SMU's six. Ethan Grunkemeyer has thrown 17 touchdowns and two interceptions, and both picks came in one night against Pitt. He won't hand Kevin Jennings free possessions, which puts the game on Brent Pry's defense. That group made 13 tackles for loss at Clemson, and it won't need half that many Friday if it gets off the field on third down. Friday won't be a rout, but I think the Hokies give the Mustangs their first home loss in the ACC. Final score prediction: Virginia Tech 30, SMU 28 THOMAS HUGHES: Let's get this out of the way: SMU has never lost an ACC game at home. Its strongest wins at Gerald J. Ford Stadium this season, however, came against Virginia and California - two squads with a combined 7-11 (4-8 ACC) record. The Hokies should be well-equipped to contend with the Mustangs, though SMU signal-caller Kevin Jennings may present Tech with its toughest test of the season yet. Virginia Tech quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer has been stellar this campaign, throwing 17 touchdowns to just two interceptions, and while I expect another strong performance from him, I think SMU narrowly edges Virginia Tech in Dallas tonight. Final score prediction: SMU 31, Virginia Tech 28 KADEN REINHARD: I think this game will be defined by one word over the 60 minutes of action: Intensity. Several factors will fuel that fire: Friday night lights, the Mustangs coming off the Syracuse loss and Tech finding itself back in the receiving-votes category of the AP Top 25. But most importantly, I see both offenses locking into a close-knit battle, as both sides can mend their attacks with a healthy mix of the ground and air attack. Ultimately, I think the Hokies' defense can handle the contest by not allowing SMU quarterback Kevin Jennings to extend many plays outside the pocket, which has been a struggle for the Hokies in recent years. Opponents complete 62.6% of their passes and average 6.0 yards per attempt. The one real hole is at safety. SMU has played two games without him: a 59-20 win over Cal and the loss at Syracuse. Help could be coming. Ahmaad Moses, a first-team All-ACC safety in 2025, is questionable after missing the whole season while SMU works on his eligibility. The junior tight end has 50 catches for 493 yards and six touchdowns, and his 50 catches lead all FBS tight ends. The last three games have been quieter: 13 catches for 120 yards since Pitt. Friday, he clears 100 receiving yards for the third time this season and finds the end zone again. 2. The Utes have cruised to an 8-0 record, winning six of their eight games by at least two touchdowns. Last week, they thrashed Cincinnati 49-25 behind 534 yards of offense. BYU has been shaky since stunning Notre Dame in Provo, losing in double-overtime to UCF and only beating lowly Arizona State by one touchdown last week. But with wins over Arizona and the Fighting Irish, the College Football Playoff resume still stacks up with the best. The Holy War has been a streaky rivalry over the years. BYU dominated the LaVell Edwards era, winning 19 of 21 matchups. Then starting in 2002, the rivalry moved heavily towards the Utes, with a 14-3 mark. BYU has now won three straight since 2021, including both matchups as members of the Big 12 by a combined four points. The 2026 game could be an all-time classic. BYU vs. Utah: Need to know Diverse offense: Utah brought in offensive coordinator Kevin McGiven from Utah State , and the new hire has completely revamped the unit. picks.blurb: How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size How Bear Bachmeier's four INTs doomed Cougars in Holy War loss Craig Meyer, USA TODAY NETWORK · USA TODAY Sports Sat, November 7, 2026 at 4:03 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The rivalry between Utah and BYU isn't just a football game. It's a war — a Holy War, to be exact. This year, the ramifications of that Biblical clash were larger than they've ever been, at least in recent memory. And it was the Utes who were able to come away with a victory. Watch BYU vs. Utah football live with Fubo (free trial) In one of the most anticipated games of a loaded Week 10 slate of the 2026 college football season, quarterback Devon Dampier accounted for four total touchdowns, two rushing and two passing, to lift No. 4 Utah to a 28-20 victory over No. 8 BYU on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, Utah. The win was sealed with two seconds remaining, when Nate Ritchie intercepted a Bear Bachmeier desperation heave in the end zone. It was Bachmeier's fourth interception of the day, matching the BYU quarterback's total from his team's first eight games this season. More: Utah has a message for CFP, SEC and Big Ten: Deal with us now The turnovers proved to be costly on a day in which the Cougars outgained the Utes by a 391-328 margin and averaged 6.1 yards per play. The win kept Utah's unbeaten record intact, improving the Utes to 9-0 overall and 6-0 in the Big 12 heading into a big game next week at No. 22 Arizona. The victory snapped Utah's three-game Holy War losing streak and was their first win in the rivalry since 2019. BYU, meanwhile, fell to 7-2 overall and 4-2 in the Big 12, narrowing its path to the Big 12 championship game and a spot in the College Football Playoff. Get real-time updates, scoring plays, turning points and expert analysis throughout as BYU takes on Utah. Follow along as USA TODAY Sports provides live updates, highlights, injury news, key plays and instant breakdown from the Cougars-Utes showdown. Utah-BYU analysis As painful as it would have been, Utah could have afforded to withstand a loss to BYU, thanks to an 8-0 start to the season that gave coach Morgan Scalley's team enough cushion to make a Big 12 championship game or College Football Playoff appearance even without an unbeaten record. But after three losses in a row to the Cougars in a series in which they hadn't won since 2019, the Utes really needed this one. And even beyond the bragging rights they earned with a 28-20 victory, they got a win that will resonate. With just three games remaining in the regular season, Utah is 9-0, with only one game left against a team that's in the top 25 of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Thanks to the win over the Cougars — which was made possible at least in some part by Bear Bachmeier's four interceptions — the Utes have a two-game lead for the second and final spot in the Big 12 championship game. To make things sweeter, by beating BYU, they significantly narrowed the Cougars' playoff chances, though a road to the 12-team field is certainly there. A big win in front of a home crowd to boost your own championship aspirations while putting your hated foes' on life support? It's what rivalry dreams are made of. And today, Utah gets to live them. Bear Bachmeier grade The BYU quarterback made some plays when he needed to and played a key role in helping the Cougars withstand an early 14-point deficit to score 20 unanswered points. His 75-yard touchdown pass to Legend Glasker in the second quarter was a thing of beauty. Beyond that, Bachmeier had a nightmarish game. The sophomore was the primary reason why a team that racked up nearly 400 yards and averaged 6.1 yards per play is nursing the wounds of a rivalry loss. Bachmeier threw four interceptions, matching his total from his first eight games this season. Each of his four picks came in Utah territory, two of which were in the Utes' red zone and one of which was on a third-and-goal from the 2-yard line with 4:39 remaining that, had he not made that mistake, would have given his team one more shot at a potential game-tying touchdown. Devon Dampier grade In some ways, Dampier was the opposite of Bachmeier. His overall stat line wasn't particularly impressive. He completed only 54% of his passes (though he was the victim of several drops by his wideouts), averaged just 6.8 yards per attempt and threw for nearly 100 fewer yards than his BYU counterpart. But he was an absolute force on the ground, racking up a game-high 87 yards and giving his team a reliable option to pick up yards when the passing game wasn't working. He accounted for each of Utah's four touchdowns, with two rushing and two passing scores. He even came up with an impressive catch on a trick play on a fourth-and-1 from the BYU 45-yard line. No. 7 BYU visits No. 3 Utah on Saturday, November 7, in the first Holy War where both teams are ranked in the top 10. The 10 a.m. local kickoff at Rice-Eccles Stadium adds another wrinkle. Utah is 8–0 and sits atop the Big 12 at 5–0. BYU is 7–1 and shares second place with Texas Tech, but its loss to UCF leaves little room for error. Utah opened as roughly a 5.5-point favorite with a total of 48.5. These predictions go against the safe script, a ground-game surprise, a Utah quarterback performance and a late BYU rally that falls short. Let's take a look at the bold predictions for this marquee matchup. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) LJ Martin plays, but Bear Bachmeier is the star Rob Gray-Imagn Images LJ Martin will return and play a limited role, yet Bachmeier will be the one who carries BYU's offense. Martin has missed four games with a leg injury and has not played since the October 3 win over TCU. He is still BYU's leading rusher at 344 yards and 7.8 yards per carry, so the Cougars badly need him. But offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said Martin is "not all the way back yet," which suggests a managed workload. The prediction is Bachmeier throws for 275 yards and rushes for two touchdowns, outproducing Martin in every category. Bachmeier has already accounted for most of BYU's rushing output without Martin, with 336 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns on 80 carries. He also has 1,750 passing yards and 12 touchdowns. Utah's secondary is among the best in the country, so BYU may need Martin's presence as a decoy more than as a workhorse. That could open play-action and RPO looks for Bachmeier. Devon Dampier and Wayshawn Parker combine for 300 total yards Utah's offense will hinge on its quarterback and running back, and together they will account for 300 total yards and four touchdowns. Dampier has been outstanding, with 12 total touchdowns against one interception over his last four games. He has completed 69.6 percent of his passes for 1,876 yards and 18 touchdowns this season. Parker is the other half. He has 726 rushing yards and nine touchdowns, and Utah's ground game ranks eighth nationally at 226.9 yards per game. BYU's rush defense is strong in raw yardage, ranking 20th at 100 yards per game, but Covers notes it ranks only 74th in rush success rate. That gap suggests Utah can win with misdirection and efficiency instead of pure power. The Utes also rank third nationally in third-down efficiency at 54.1 percent, which helps them sustain drives against an aggressive linebacker group. Utah will lose right tackle Kelvin Obot for the season, but the line has still been one of the best in the country. I expect the Utes to handle his absence. Utah wins 31–27 and snaps BYU's three-game streak The final prediction is a four-point Utah win that comes down to the last possession. BYU has won three straight in the series, while Utah had won nine in a row before that. Utah has still won 14 straight overall, the longest active streak in the FBS. Utah's offense should control the game early, but BYU will keep it close by converting in the red zone. A late Cougars touchdown will make it a one-possession game before the Utes' defense finishes with a stop. The projected 58 total points would clear the 48.5-point line comfortably. The point spread would also come down to a single score, giving BYU a cover as a 5.5-point underdog. The result would leave Utah in prime position for a Big 12 title game berth and a playoff bid. BYU would stay alive in the conference race, but it would have almost no margin left. Backup running back Preston Rex missed last weeks game and Sione Moa has been just OK running the ball. Prior to the injury, Martin has rushed for 344 yards and has three scores on the year, and is averaging a monster 7.8 yards per carry this year. home.headline: BYU releases initial LJ Martin injury status ahead of Utah game
home.blurb: On Wednesday night, the BYU football program provided the first official injury update for LJ Martin ahead of a top 10 matchup with Utah. Martin is "doubtful" for the game against the Utes. The "doubtful" designation is reserved for the players that have a 25% chance to play. However, just a few minutes before the injury report came out, ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Martin is considered "questionable" for this weekend. The "questionable" designation is reserved for players with a 50% chance to play. Thamel reported that if Martin returns, "he's not expected to be 100% and could be limited." Thamel added more information, saying "[Martin is] trending to dress, be available, and have some impact on the game. A final decision will be made later this week." Martin was back practicing on Tuesday, according to Aaron Roderick. The last time he played was in early October against TCU. If Martin can't go, BYU will turn to Preston Rex who was not available for the ASU game. Rex had a breakout game against Notre Dame before suffering an injury against UCF. If Saleapaga isn't available, expect more sets with three wide receivers. That would leave Walker Lyons on the field for most of the game. If Evan Johnson can't play, BYU will turn to Jayven Williams and Therrian Alexander III at cornerback. Williams and Alexander shut down two of the best wide receivers in the Big 12 last week. They are more than capable of holding it down on the outside. The bigger question will be who BYU plays at nickel. The Cougars started Cannon DeVries at that spot to start the season, but DeVries has primarily been used for punt return duties since he suffered an injury. The ASU game was the first time DeVries had seen defensive snaps since suffering the injury. He played 14 snaps. LJ Martin and Evan Johnson Officially Ruled Out for BYU Against ASU If Martin returns, it would be the first time BYU has had its full compliment of running backs since the season opener. Other Injury Updates on BYU Starters BYU also provided injury updates on key starters Roger Saleapaga and Evan Johnson. Saleapaga left the game against ASU with an injury, and Johnson suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury against UCF. Johnson did not play against Arizona State last weekend. Most of the time, BYU had three safeties on the field. BYU averaged 2.7 safeties on the field at a time against ASU. True freshman Kennan Pula has seen his role grow over the last few weeks. He played 24 snaps against the Sun Devils. The Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) have already blown out league foes Florida and Texas A&M at home this season and are 13-3 at Faurot Field against league opposition since 2023. Taking on Texas (6-2, 3-2) represents an uptick in competition, but the Tigers shouldn't be lacking confidence. Florida was No. 8 in the AP poll when it arrived at Mizzou on Oct. 3. It left with a 45-17 loss that legitimized Missouri and showed its full potential. Since then, we've also seen Missouri's floor, which was found in a 31-3 loss at Ole Miss on Oct. 17. But after a bye week and a 34-10 "get right" win over Arkansas in Week 9, the Tigers appear to be back on track. The Longhorns are entering off wins over Ole Miss and Mississippi State , but their vaunted offense is still falling short of expectations. Is this the point when everything will start to click for quarterback Arch Manning ? If a Texas team that spent four weeks at No. 1 earlier this season is going to meet expectations, a breakthrough needs to come soon. Where to watch Texas vs. Missouri live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Faurot Field -- Columbia, Missouri TV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Texas vs. Missouri: Need to know Injuries mount for Texas: Injuries are adding up for the Longhorns, who enter this matchup with star receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman listed as questionable. Wingo is dealing with a quad injury while Coleman is working through a shoulder issue. Both have appeared in all eight games for Texas up to this point while combining to catch 11 of Arch Manning's 15 touchdown passes. Star edge rusher Collin Simmons is also questionable after missing Texas' past two games because of an ankle injury. That's a lot of star power in the "questionable" category for Texas. By contrast, Missouri's injury report is nearly clean. Welcome back, Ahmad: Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy made his 2026 debut last week, carrying the football twice in the Tigers' win over Arkansas. The 2025 All-American has been on the mend from a gunshot wound, and his return adds to a running back room that already features the SEC's leading rusher. Jamal Roberts became the conference's first back to surpass 1,000 yards for the season while rushing for 138 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries in a win over Arkansas. Roberts surpassed 200 yards in wins over Florida and Texas A&M last month. Gaining traction against Texas will be tough. No team has averaged more than four yards per rush attempt against Texas. College Football playoff implications: Texas' chance to reach the College Football Playoff will improve to 67.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFB Forecaster. They will drop to 22.8% with a loss. If the Longhorns lose, they would need to win out against LSU, Arkansas and Texas A&M in order to potentially reach the 12-team field as a three-loss team. Missouri's chances to make the CFP will improve to 16.1% with a win. Those hopes would crater to 1.6% with a loss. The Tigers close with Georgia , Kentucky and Oklahoma . Texas vs. Missouri prediction, picks The best unit on this field is the Texas defense. Regardless of the health status of star edge rusher Collin Simmons, the Longhorns should be able to slow down a Missouri offense that hasn't faced a swarming unit of this caliber. If Arch Manning can just take care of the football like he did last week, Texas can lean on its defense, win the field position battle and put stress on a Missouri defense that showed real vulnerability in losses to Mississippi State and Ole Miss. The Tigers have been great at home the last few years, but they are a rung below Texas in overall talent level. Staff Picks and Scores Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB After getting to play their entire October slate in the Lone Star State, the Longhorns are once again leaving town for Columbia, Missouri, to take on the No. 18 Missouri Tigers. While fans may already be looking ahead to next week's highly anticipated Death Valley matchup, the Tigers are certainly not a team to overlook . They're coming off a 34-10 blowout win over Arkansas — albeit, it was against the Razorbacks — and steamrolled the same Florida team that stunned Texas with a second-half comeback just a few weeks ago. Saturday's matchup carries significant postseason implications , both for the College Football Playoff and the SEC championship race, as both teams enter with identical 3-2 conference records. Here’s how the Texas Longhorns On SI Staff sees this one playing out. Matt Galatzan Texas has gotten back on track over the last two weeks, but various shortcoming are still very prevelent. Texas has struggled along offensive line, and as a result, the running game has suffered. Those issues have also caused a cascading effect on the passing game, making for an inconsistent product. To make things worse, things on the injury front don't look good for the Horns. Kade Phillips, Ryan Wingo and Graceson Littleton are all banged up but should play, while Colin Simmons and Cam Coleman are less likely to play, and Hollywood Smothers and Nick Townsend were both lost for the year. Texas can overcome these issues if the defense continues to perform at a high level. Ole Miss showed the blueprint to shut down the Tigers ' offense. If Texas can stay on schedule on offense and avoid a third-quarter collapse, I think they can get it done. Texas 27, Missouri 20 Phoenix Haigis Texas has started to find their groove again with two major wins at home against Ole Miss and Mississippi State. The Longhorns now go back on the road against another ranked opponent in Missouri. As much momentum as Texas has going into this game, all the advantages matchup-wise go in favor of the Tigers. Texas is dealing with a significant amount of major injuries with the addition of running back Hollywood Smothers being out for the season while Missouri will see their running back Ahmad Hardy return for the first time this season. The Tigers are one of the best teams at home this year and have the best turnover margin in the SEC against a Lorghorns team that has had turnover issues this season. picks.blurb: Greg McElroy Predicts Missouri Upset That Could Shake Texas' Playoff Hopes Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS ESPN analyst Greg McElroy believes Texas’ turnover problems will catch up with the Longhorns at Missouri, making the Tigers his lone outright upset pick of Week 10 as both 6-2 SEC teams fight to stay in the College Football Playoff race. McElroy backed the Tigers on his Always College Football podcast, predicting a low-scoring game decided by ball security. “The team that gives it away just one time, that’s the team that’s going to lose,” he said. Why is Greg McElroy picking Missouri? Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz reacts toward a referee during the first quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” “Missouri is +8 in turnover margin. Texas is -3,” McElroy said. “That’s probably the clearest season-long difference between these two teams.” The Tigers turned four Arkansas turnovers into 24 points in last week’s win in Fayetteville, and Missouri coach Eli Drinkwitz said afterward that “turnovers are the name of the game .” McElroy added that Missouri has scored 62 points off takeaways this season without allowing a point off a giveaway. “So when his team wins the turnover battle by one or more, Eli Drinkwitz is 39-4,” McElroy said. Texas checked in at No. 7 in the first College Football Playoff rankings , 11 spots ahead of Missouri. Still, both Missouri losses came on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, two teams Texas beat over the last two weeks. Arch Manning’s costly turnover trouble Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on after a medical check during the game against Ole Miss | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Texas quarterback Arch Manning has 15 touchdown passes and averages 8 yards per attempt, but McElroy flagged his seven interceptions as a problem against a team that “cashes mistakes in very, very quickly.” Both Texas losses came by three points and turned on fourth-quarter turnovers, including a pick-six against Oklahoma and a strip-sack with under two minutes left against Florida. Mississippi State sacked the redshirt junior six times last Saturday, and Texas now plays without left tackle Trevor Goosby, who suffered a season-ending knee injury against Ole Miss. “They average getting sacked nearly one out of every 10 dropbacks,” McElroy said of Texas. “That’s 126th because the breakdowns come from all over the protection.” The ESPN analyst said Texas has struggled when its receivers have to beat man coverage snap after snap, and he called Missouri’s cornerbacks “about as good as you find when it comes to playing that coverage week in and week out.” How does Texas reach 24 points? Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian celebrates with fans and players after the game against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” McElroy questioned how Texas coach Steve Sarkisian’s offense gets there. “When his team scores fewer than 24 points, Steve Sarkisian is 14-35,” McElroy said. “And Texas already goes three-and-out on more than a quarter of their possessions.” The Longhorns’ running game offers little relief, with McElroy saying their backs “are getting hit almost as soon as they take the handoff.” Running back Hollywood Smothers is out, and receivers Ryan Wingo and Cam Coleman were both listed as questionable on Thursday’s SEC availability report . Wingo, a St. Louis native Missouri recruited out of high school, leads Texas with 36 catches for 470 yards, while Coleman, an Auburn transfer, leads the team with seven touchdown catches. McElroy’s route to 24 points runs through Wingo “in the catch-and-run game” against a Missouri defense he said sits “at or near the bottom as far as missed tackles,” plus “one Coleman shot over the top.” “But without it, Texas might be living on field goals, which is a dangerous recipe on the road,” McElroy said. A loss would send Texas to LSU next week with three defeats, a scenario ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum said could cause the Longhorns to “ collapse .” Texas visits Missouri at noon ET Saturday on ESPN. That meeting was the 2017 Texas Bowl. What should scare Longhorns fans is the 2026 version is tinkering on the edge of a disappointing bowl like that. Especially if they can't beat a team like Missouri. The Tigers are a good team. It's easy to see Missouri winning on Saturday. They're ranked just 11 spots below Texas in the College Football Playoff rankings and have the same record. And Mizzou has home field advantage. Then why is Texas a -3.5-point favorite. Because a fully functioning Texas team is better than Missouri. But this Texas team isn't fully functioning. First, the injuries are starting to pile up. It was announced this week that the Longhorns have lost running back Hollywood Smothers and tight end Nick Townsend for the rest of the season. All-American right tackle Trevor Goosby is also out for the year. And UT has been without All-American EDGE Colin Simmons for weeks. In addition to trying to plug the injury holes, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian must also continue to work on the offense. At times it looks great. But its not trustworthy. Will Muschamp's defense will need to stand tall for a third game in a row if the offense can't get it going. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas walks into this Missouri game needing the win to feel confident about their CFP chance heading into LSU. Missouri is a relative unknown, with losses to both Mississippi schools but a dominating win over Florida. Jamal Roberts and the run game leads the way, averaging just over 160 rushing yards/game. Austin Simmons has become a riser in this upcoming NFL Draft, flashing his elite arm talent every week. Texas was able to get a win over Tennessee earlier this season, but I don't see this as a task that's comparable. Missouri is capable of performing at a high level on both sides of the ball, especially the front seven defensively. It's difficult to imagine this Texas offense to trade punches with Missouri, especially on the road, so I'll take the Tigers to possibly end Texas' CFP hopes. Final Score: Texas 20, Missouri 23 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns will take on Missouri this Saturday in their latest SEC clash. The Tigers are off to an impressive 6-2 start and, like Texas, are 3-2 in conference play. Texas will need Arch Manning to be at his best and for the defense to shine. Last week, the Longhorns defense held Mississippi State to three points and 187 total yards. If the Longhorns can replicate that performance, another win could be on the horizon. This should be a game that Texas can win as they look to improve their playoff odds. Final Score: Texas 31, Missouri 13 Trey Luerssen's Prediction When this year's schedule came out, I thought the game against Mizzou might be the toughest to forecast. But it's even tougher now, because we're not sure which team will actually show up on either side of the ball. Both teams have had some big wins and some real clunkers. How much will Texas miss Smothers and Townsend? Can the defense slow down the Tigers offense? Which version of quarterback Arch Manning will show up in Columbia? For four games in a row, Texas has jumped out to an early lead and then coughed it up by the end of the third quarter. UT is 2-2 in that stretch. A coin flip. Twice the dam broke and twice it didn't. I think the defense will save the offense again. That was a devastating result after Trevor Goosby — a pillar of the Longhorns' offensive line who is projected to be a top-10 pick in next year's draft — had already been ruled out for the remainder of the year. The injuries for Texas could be the straw that breaks the camel's back, with the Longhorns already struggling on offense, limping into Week 10 ranked 74th in Success Rate, 95th in Explosiveness and 129th in Havoc Allowed. Arch Manning's inconsistencies have made it difficult for Texas to stay ahead of the sticks, leaving the offense vulnerable to stalling out early on in drives. While Coleman and Wingo are expected to play at less than 100%, Smothers' outlook looks bleak, forcing the Longhorns to lean more heavily on Raleek Brown . When given the opportunity, Brown has been a consistent source of production in the Texas backfield, averaging nearly five yards per carry. With question marks lingering over the offense, the Longhorns will need to continue to play at a high level on the other side of the ball in order to keep their hopes of making the playoffs alive. Luckily for Texas, the defense has been the strength of the team this season, entering Week 10 ranked in the top 25 in Success Rate, Explosiveness, Finishing Drives and Havoc. Missouri 's hot start to the year is arguably one of the bigger surprises of the season, with the Tigers just one win away from clearing the over on their regular-season win total while sitting 1.5 games back from first in the SEC conference standings. Austin Simmons ' resurgence under center has played a major role in Missouri's success, throwing just two interceptions in eight games while averaging 8.1 yards per throw. While Simmons has been able to thrive through the air, the Tigers' running back room has yet to find its footing, ranking near the bottom of the board in Rush Success Rate and PPA. When Jamal Roberts is unable to hit the ground running, opposing defenses can stretch out their linebackers across the middle, smothering Simmons' passing lanes at multiple levels of the field. It is worth noting Ahmad Hardy was able to make his return to the field after suffering a scary gunshot wound in the offseason, potentially giving Missouri the spark it needs to be a well-rounded offense. While his return was welcome to see, expectations will need to be tempered, with the Tigers' running back being held to just two carries. Like Texas, Missouri has also built its success on the shoulders of the defense, fielding a group that ranks 29th in Success Rate and fifth in Havoc. While the Tigers do give up explosive plays at an alarming rate, they are able to successfully keep their opponents out of the end zone, giving up just 3.03 Points per Opportunity. While Simmons has been able to play far better than initially expected, negative regression is looming large over the Tigers' quarterback as he battles it out against a secondary that excels in coverage, per its top-30 mark in Dropback EPA Allowed per play. With the Longhorns keeping a body on Missouri's pass-catchers' hips, the amount of Havoc in Simmons' throws will increase, leading to an uptick in his total number of Turnover-Worthy Plays. Even with Hardy back on the field, it's tough to envision the star running back being able to quickly shake off the rust, making the Tigers far too one-dimensional. Barring a sudden turnaround on the ground, Texas will be able to drop more bodies back in coverage, making it easier to create disruptions. Colin Simmons has also been upgraded to questionable, yet it remains to be seen if the Longhorns' edge rusher will suit up on Saturday. While the Longhorns do generate pressure at a high rate, Simmons would help pull defensive attention to the edge, freeing up more space in the interior to help the middle of the defensive line collapse the pocket. With no clear path for success, expect Missouri to be held to early outs at a consistent rate, chipping away at the Tigers' total number of scoring opportunities. Then the Red Raiders lost Coy Eakin to a broken hand in this past week's win over West Virginia. The Texas Tech football team's receiver room has been the most impacted by injury this season, and that continues to be the case. We'll move some guys around, like Bryson Jones. He'll get some slot along with getting some outside, which he has." Campbell took Eakin's place as the slot receiver after the veteran departed the West Virginia game in the first quarter. The Frenship grad had a pair of catches for 56 yards against the Mountaineers. McGuire also said players like Leyton Stone and Imari Jehiel could also see some action. He also wants to keep Simmons as an outside receiver when he returns to action. home.blurb: Mizzou published its first of four SEC-mandated availability and injury reports on Wednesday, Nov. 4, ahead of its game this coming Saturday against Texas, and added no new names to begin the week. That marks the second straight week that the Tigers have opened a game week without any injury concerns beyond players previously ruled out for the year. The major injury news comes out of Austin, Texas, as the Longhorns listed multiple starters and key players with availability designations. On offense for Texas, starting wideouts Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo were listed as questionable, and rotational running back Hollywood Smothers has been ruled out. On defense for the Longhorns, star defensive end Colin Simmons is questionable. Starting nickel Graceson Littleton and cornerback Kade Phillips, who have played the fifth- and sixth-most defensive snaps for the Longhorns this season, respectively, also were questionable. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. Tony Liebert: Minnesota 21, UCLA 14 P.J. Fleck has a track record of performing well as a home underdog, and he has a great chance to add to that narrative this week against UCLA. The Bruins haven't played on the road since sneaking past Oregon for their best win on Oct. 10. The only thing that scares me for the Gophers' chances this week is a hangover after last week's emotional loss to Indiana, but I expect Fleck's team to be ready to end UCLA's perfect season. Joe Nelson: Minnesota 21, UCLA 17 I don't want to say UCLA doesn't deserve to be ranked in the top 10, but who have they actually beaten to prove they're legit? Oregon without Dante Moore? Please. Minnesota has proven it's almost good enough to beat anyone, losing a brutal 23-16 heartbreaker to Indiana last week. There's no real mystery to what UCLA does. It blasts away, with the ground game, gets just enough from the passing game to get by, and then it relies on the defense to take care of everything else. It starts with third down stops. Only Nebraska – at least before the loss to Illinois – is better at defensively on third downs than the Bruins. That allows UCLA to dominate the time of possession battle, the rested defense forces a ton of takeaways, the offense capitalizes … repeat. However … Why Minnesota Will Win UCLA runs well, Minnesota doesn't. Minnesota can throw well, UCLA doesn't. Other than that, these two do almost all of the same things. You want third down defense? Minnesota is sixth in the nation, allowing teams to convert just 28% of their chances. Time of possession? Print (Opens in new window) Print Best of OC: Winners in every category Lawyer accused of misappropriation How a small victory during a midweek practice became a gain for both the wide receiver and the cornerback in the Bruins’ road win against Minnesota last weekend LOS ANGELES — One catch by UCLA wide receiver Aidan Mizell against cornerback Scooter Jackson last Tuesday morning set the stage for what was to come on Saturday afternoon in Minneapolis. Mizell caught a pair of 75-yard touchdown passes from Ty Dieffenbach in Saturday’s 34-20 victory over the Golden Gophers on a day when Dieffenbach threw for a career-high 303 yards on just eight completions and Jackson came up with interception as the Bruins improved to 9-0 for the first time since 1999. Jackson dropped back and maneuvered in front of wide receiver Jalen Smith for his interception of Minnesota quarterback Drake Lindsey. “You guys see it every day in practice,” Jackson said. “Those guys, and when I say ‘those guys’ it’s not just Aidan. It’s Brian (Rowe Jr.), Semaj (Morgan), and I can keep going on and on. Those guys every day make me better. You see it in practice. They do me up in practice every day. But on Saturdays, they help me perform very well.” The kind of plays like the ones seen last Tuesday are an example of how and why UCLA is finding ways to win each week. That day, it was Jackson victimized by a highlight-reel grab from Mizell in practice. Dieffenbach threw a high, arcing pass that Jackson misread. Jackson’s hands became entangled in the pads of Mizell, who had beaten him down the field with his route. The ball spiraled toward Mizell, who made an acrobatic catch and sent his offensive teammates into celebration. There wasn’t a negative reaction by either side. Mizell didn’t taunt Jackson, and Jackson didn’t react negatively. It was just two players going back and forth at each other, who, in the process of challenging each other, have helped transform UCLA in their own way. “That’s what we talked about being the standards of our team,” said UCLA head coach Bob Chesney, who is getting his Bruins (9-0, 6-0 Big Ten) ready to take on Illinois (6-3, 4-2) on Friday night. “There’s probably eight or nine bullet points at the beginning of the year, and we review every Friday and make sure those are important. When you get to the game, and you put yourself in a position where you’ve been there before. You’ve competed against someone who is of equal caliber to you. Sometimes Aidan is going to get Scooter, and sometimes Scooter is going to get Aidan.” Practices that become competitive on Tuesdays and Wednesdays produce moments that count when Jackson and Mizell are in the same uniform and cheering each other. “There’s something better than that type of competition for them to go against each other,” Chesney said. “That little bit of success breeds a little bit more confidence. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 5 Alabama is out to defend its College Football Playoff ranking, while No. 14 LSU seeks to remain in the hunt Getty Images One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss ' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race. Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State , South Carolina and Mississippi State . The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown , adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form : No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii , Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots : When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State . Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Our Alabama vs. LSU prediction and college football picks back Lane Kiffin and the Tigers to snap their Saban Bowl losing streak as Alabama seeks its fourth straight series victory on the first Saturday in November. The Crimson Tide visit Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La., where LSU enters as a 5. 5-point favorite in Death Valley. Kickoff is scheduled for 3: 30 p. m. ET on ABC on Saturday, Nov. 7. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs LSU: LSU -5.5 The last time LSU won the Saban Bowl, Nick Saban was Alabama's head coach and Lane Kiffin was still beloved at Ole Miss . That will change Saturday when Kiffin's surging Tigers take advantage of a Crimson Tide team that's looked like a far cry from its No. 5 College Football Playoff ranking. With LSU's defensive ferocity and Alabama's offensive struggles, I like the Tigers to cover up to -6.5 at home against the Tide. Not only has LSU's defense been wrecking opponents, but the Tigers' offense has been on fire too, with Sam Leavitt fourth nationally in QBR (85.3) and 12th in adjusted completion percentage (79.5%). Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris (480 receiving yards and seven TDs in his last four SEC games) are a problem for an Alabama defense that's ranked 78th in pass success rate (44.3%). Alabama vs LSU Over/Under pick: Under 52.5 This game isn't one of the must-watch games in my college football Top 25 predictions this week because I'm expecting offensive fireworks; it's because of the talent on these defenses. LSU's defense is especially loaded, and with Alabama's struggles against quality defenses, I would play the Under at 51.5 or better. The Tigers are second nationally in sacks (34) , and Keelon Russell hasn't managed pressure well. He's been sacked the ninth-most in the country (22) and has a 20.4% pressure-to-sack rate. But I don't expect an offensive onslaught from LSU either. This is the best defense the Tigers have faced this season, with Alabama ranking 20th nationally in available yards percentage (37.7%) and 14th in net adjusted EPA per play. Alabama vs LSU prop: Alabama TT Under 23.5 Alabama's offense has no identity, and Kalen DeBoer and Ryan Grubb don't seem to know how to fix it. The Crimson Tide have faced two high-quality defenses this season and failed to score more than 17 points in both games. Against LSU, I like the Under on the Crimson Tide's team total at 21.5 or better . Alabama continues to deal with two key injuries on the offensive side of the ball, with both center Racin Delgatty and wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams questionable for this game. If those two don't play, Alabama will struggle to score even 20 points. The Crimson Tide don't have consistent playmakers outside of Coleman-Williams, and LSU's defense brings the heat, ranking fourth nationally in havoc rate (22.2%) . Alabama vs LSU combo Alabama has gotten off to slow starts and failed to cover in three straight games as a result. In the Crimson Tide's last three games, it trailed Georgia 10-0, trailed Tennessee 9-0, and trailed Texas A&M 14-10. If Alabama gets off to another slow start and trails LSU, the Tigers' defense will pin their ears back and go to work. LSU ranks eighth nationally in pass success rate on defense (36%) and has one of the most lethal pass rush duos in the country, Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross (58 combined pressures and 13.5 sacks). Death Valley is one of the hardest places to play, and with Alabama's broken offense, I don't expect the Tide to score much early against this opportunistic LSU defense. A team which Alabama has won the last three games against dating back to 2023, this latest showdown against LSU is likely to be their toughest in recent years. The Tigers are considered one of the SEC's top teams at 6-2 (3-2 SEC), and have a roster loaded with talent led by head coach Lane Kiffin. In addition to that, this latest matchup between the Crimson Tide and Tigers has significant College Football Playoff (CFP) implications. Released this past Tuesday night, Alabama was ranked No. 5 in the first CFP rankings as the top ranked two-loss team, while LSU sat at No. 14. A challenging matchup, let's make three predictions for the Crimson Tide during Saturday's massive road game at LSU. Alabama's offensive line struggles against LSU pass rush Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Michael Carroll (64) waits for the snap during the third quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images When taking a look back at the Tennessee game, Alabama's offensive line struggled at times in pass protection with a Volunteers defense that led the nation in sacks, and the Tide are likely set to face a similar challenge this Saturday in a LSU unit which ranks No. 2 nationally in the stat. As a result, combined with the tough road atmosphere in Tiger Stadium, I'll predict the Alabama offensive line to struggle at times in pass protection against an elite LSU pass rush, especially if the Crimson Tide are without two starters up front. Alabama's defense forces multiple turnovers Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception during the second quarter against the Georgia Bulldogs at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt enters Week 10 leading the SEC with eight interceptions thrown this season, and is set to face an Alabama defense that has 12 picks this year which is tied atop the conference. I'll say that Alabama picks off Leavitt at-least once this Saturday afternoon, with the Tide defense also forcing a fumble at some point. Keelon Russell, Tide passing game has solid showing While I do predict Alabama's offense to struggle in pass protection at times similar to the Tennessee game, I do not think the passing game will struggle as much as it did in Knoxville where the Tide threw for only 147 yards. Yes, the Tide are facing a LSU defense that ranks No. 3 in the SEC in fewest yards allowed per game, but Alabama might be getting Ryan Coleman-Williams back Saturday, and with an extra week of rest and preparation, I would imagine we see a different performance from Keelon Russell and company. The loser of this game may miss out on the college football playoff and given the Tigers' remaining strength of schedule, this is a must-win for LSU. Both teams are coming off a bye week, so we should expect a chess match between Lane Kiffin and Kalen DeBoer . Some would say this is a must-win for Alabama despite being the #5 ranked team in the new playoff rankings. The Tide's two best wins came against Kentucky when the Wildcats were unranked and a routing of #16 Mississippi State which sent Kamario Taylor and the program into a spiral. A win at LSU would solidify Alabama's spot, but a loss puts their season in the hands of others. Alabama plays Vanderbilt, Chattanooga, and Auburn following LSU; one of the easiest strength of schedules in P4. Alabama trailed 20-17 to Texas A&M before rattling off 14 points in the fourth quarter to avoid three-straight losses. Keelon Russell threw for 311 yards and three touchdowns, and the defense forced three turnovers in the win. Alabama has won three straight against LSU and won 12 of the last 15. Sam Leavitt and Kiffin will try to break the streak in his debut season. LSU is coming off two back-to-back big wins before the bye week. The Tigers crushed Mississippi State 31-0 and Auburn 38-17. Sam Leavitt threw seven touchdowns and ran for another in that two-game span, plus Jackson Harris caught four of those touchdowns and totaled 263 receiving yards. LSU's defense has only allowed 281 yards through the air in those two games as well, so nothing should come easy in Death Valley for one of the best home defenses in the country. Let's dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Both Alabama and LSU come into the game with a record of 6-2, giving each team a chance to make a real statement . Each team is coming off a bye week, giving them more rest and time to prepare for this huge game. With SEC schedule changes coming, this matchup will be the last one played between the two teams on a yearly basis. This could add more emphasis for both sides to want to come away with the win. With this rivalry game kicking off in a few days, the Crimson Tide aren't being favored to come away with the win on the road. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Alabama only has a 43 percent chance of taking down LSU this week. Since the game is being played on the road, LSU is likely being favored, especially since Tiger Stadium can be so tough to play in. One of the bigger keys to the game for the Crimson Tide will be how quarterback Keelon Russell can perform. Alabama has all the confidence in the world in Russell, but he has been a little shaky at times this season. For the year, the signal-caller has thrown for 2,057 yards with 15 touchdowns and five interceptions through the air. On the ground, Russell has made his presence known for this team, rushing for Russell has proven to be very impactful for Alabama, even with his limited experience as a starting quarterback. If Russell can handle the hostile atmosphere that LSU will throw at him, the Crimson Tide could have a strong chance to win the game. Alabama is going to need Russell to play more like he did against Kentucky earlier in the season, rather than how he looked against Tennessee a few weeks ago. The signal-caller have a lot of talent, but he can sometimes make poor decisions with the football. LSU has a very strong defense, and this will be a major challenge for Russell to overcome this week. But if Alabama is going to reach the heights that this program wants to get to this season, Russell is going to have to be able to handle these types of games. Kickoff for the final yearly meeting between the two rivals is set for 12:30 p.m. PT/3:30 p.m. ET from Baton Rouge.

It's possible that the loser of this game could still get into the playoff with three losses — it depends on how the rest of the season plays out — but the winner will be the only one that controls its own destiny moving forward. ESPN's Greg McElroy, a former Alabama quarterback, made his score prediction for the game, and he has LSU leaving Tiger Stadium with a 27-20 win. away.headline: Josh Ford set to miss rest of Alabama football season, per reports
away.blurb: “Josh suffered an injury, and it can be season-ending,” DeBoer said. “I mean, the guy’s so tough, I know he’s probably right now, he’s trying to figure out how he’s still gonna play this year. It’s just who he is. His impact has been really key for our football team in a lot of ways. Just a guy that’s a uniter. You’ve got uniters and dividers, I think, and he’s a uniter of our football team. He’s a leader.” Alabama tight end Josh Ford is set to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, Kalen DeBoer confirmed on Monday. Ford sustained a torn ACL late in the Crimson Tide’s 31-13 victory over LSU this past Saturday, according to the school’s NIL entity. He had caught a touchdown pass earlier in the game. Ford transferred to the Crimson Tide ahead of the 2026 season from Oklahoma State. Primarily a blocking tight end who was a tone setter, Ford also caught five passes for 41 yards and two touchdowns. CBS Sports was first to report the news. Ford already was playing through a broken bone in his arm, sustained during the Oct. 3 win over Mississippi State in Starkville. He had surgery shortly thereafter and played the following week vs. Georgia with a cast on his arm. Without Ford at tight end, Alabama still has Kaleb Edwards, Marshall Pritchett, Jay Lindsey and Danny Lewis. Pritchett and Edwards have been bigger targets in the passing game, but they and others will have to step up with Ford not able to help block. “Danny Lewis, kind of starts with him,” Alabama offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb said. “He’s your next pure inline Y or blocker ... Kaleb is obviously our guy. He’s our starting Y. I think you know I can’t say enough good about 81, and I was not surprised that he played as well as he did. I know he had the holding call on the big run that got called back, but he played a whale of a football game. And I think he’s one of the five or six tight ends in the country that are that 6-5 260-pound, true 50-50 player that can block and catch, and you know you don’t give any tells away when he’s on the field because he can do both. Think the world of Kaleb. Probably going to put a little bit more on his plate, and then, like I said, Danny Lewis is a guy that will step up certainly. And Jay Lindsey will have probably more of an expanded role as well.” The Crimson Tide (7-2, 5-2 SEC) plays at Vanderbilt on Saturday. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit al.com. home.headline: LSU football, Lane Kiffin fall to No. 9 Alabama in Week 10
home.blurb: Alabama (7-2, 5-2) played like its season depended on it, jumping out to a first-half lead and overpowering the Tigers in their own home for a 31-13 victory. Freshman quarterback Kaelon Russell put on a show, throwing for 206 yards and three touchdowns, picking LSU’s defense apart when it matter most. Despite being outgained in total yards of offense, the Crimson Tide made the most of every red zone trip they had, while the same couldn’t be said for Lane Kiffin and his Tigers. LSU ended the game going 2 out of 4 in its red zone visits, with both of those red zone trips ending in field goals instead of touchdowns. With this loss, LSU falls to .500 in conference play and possibly out of playoff contention. Kiffin and the Tigers will look to flush this one quickly with No. 10 Texas coming to town on Nov. 14. The story of this game will come down to which quarterback can perform better. Sam Leavitt has been better for the Tigers (6-2, 3-2 SEC) of late. His las time out at Auburn, he threw for 387 yards, accounted for four touchdowns but arguably more important, he didn't have a turnover. After a 32-yard punt return from Coleman-Williams, Russell only needed one play to extend Alabama's lead in the fourth quarter. The freshman signal caller dropped a dime from 25 yards out to wide receiver Cederian Morgan for a touchdown. The play only took five second off the clock, a good thing for LSU who now has even more of a hill to climb to make a comeback. LSU's defense was never in position on that drive and got burned twice. That's one of the few times all season Blake Baker's defense looked befuddled and out of place. Leavitt and company came out of the halftime looking to put points on the board. While they still have yet to taste the endzone, Leavitt and running back Dillin Jones were able to get the Tigers back in scoring position on their opening second-half drive. Staryzk capped the drive off with a 41-yard field goal to make it a four-point game. LSU football stalling out in the red zone Crimson Tide is running the ball today, something I thought would rougher for it to do against LSU. Alabama is winning one of the one-on-one battles when LSU's defense is out there right now. LSU faced a fourth and long to start the second quarter and elected to trust in Staryzk's foot to give it the lead. Staryzk attempted a field goal from 56 yards out and pushed it far left for his first miss of the day. With both the Tigers (6-3, 3-3 SEC) and Crimson Tide entering the matchup with two losses, losing on Saturday Nov. 7, inside Tiger Stadium wasn’t an option if either team wanted to solidify themselves as a possible College Football Playoff team.
