LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 12 Ohio State hosts No. 23 Oregon in a pivotal game in the Big Ten and CFP race Getty Images Week 10 of the college football season has been highlighted since the schedule was released, with No. 23 Oregon's trip to face No. 12 Ohio State among the headliners. However, when the Buckeyes host the Ducks at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS, it will not be two teams vying for a bye in the College Football Playoff, but instead two programs trying to keep their season from unraveling. The Ducks, at 5-3, have already seen their playoff dreams snuffed out, but a win last week against Northwestern brought their offense to life after a coordinator change. Dylan Raiola had his best game as a starter for Oregon in a win over Northwestern, and now the Ducks have real belief they can go into the Horseshoe and pick up a win that could salvage what's been a disappointing season. Ohio State, meanwhile, comes in with a backup quarterback of their own and is searching for answers after a 30-18 loss on the road to USC last week. Luke Fahey will get his second start and first at home, hoping to find more success and keep Ohio State in the playoff hunt after the first CFP rankings put them at No. 12 -- which would be the first team out of the 12-team playoff. The winner on Saturday will enter the stretch run of the season feeling like they've stabilized after a shock to the system in the form of losing their star quarterbacks for the year. The loser, on the other hand, will realize their goals are no longer within reach and face some hard questions entering the offseason. Where to watch Ohio State vs. Oregon live Date : Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time : 3:30 p.m. ET Location : Ohio Stadium -- Columbus, Ohio TV: CBS | Live stream: CBSSports.com , CBS Sports App Streaming on Paramount+ Premium Ohio State vs. Oregon: Need to know Can Ohio State solve red-zone woes?: The Buckeyes moved the ball fine against USC's defense. It was the best rushing performance from Ohio State this season in Big Ten play in terms of yards per carry (4.74), and while Fahey missed some explosives, he still threw for 260 yards. The problem for Ohio State was finishing drives with six points instead of three. Ohio State made four trips into the red zone against USC and came away with just 13 points. Against Indiana , it also scored 13 points in three trips to the red zone, and the inability to come away with touchdowns nearly cost them there too. If the Buckeyes are going to control this game and keep Oregon from building belief it can win on the road, Fahey has to be sharper in the red zone and the Ohio State rushing attack has to be able to help out. Ducks find life after coordinator change: Oregon's offense had its best performance since the win at USC last Saturday afternoon against Northwestern, one week after firing offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer. Interim coordinator Jay Johnson seemed able to get Raiola into a rhythm and keep him there, something the Ducks have struggled with all season (even with Dante Moore ). The frustration after the Illinois game seemed to be an unwillingness to stick with what worked -- in that game, it was the rushing attack -- and against Northwestern, once they found some concepts that worked, they went back to the well until proven otherwise. That seems simple, but it's not always easy as a play-caller to not let your mind wander and get too cute trying to stay ahead of the defense. Johnson seems more comfortable just rolling with what works and being aggressive in any spot, which seems to have a trickle-down effect on Raiola and the offense, also playing with more comfort and aggression. That's going to be necessary against an Ohio State defense that is quite good but, as USC proved, can be hit for big plays. Oregon can't be afraid to take swings as a road dog, and last week's performance gives it some confidence it can do that effectively with Raiola. Which defense can steal possessions?: With a young quarterback and a red-zone offense that's struggling, the Buckeyes might need their defense to give them a spark. For as good as the Buckeyes have been defensively this season, they haven't been great at turning teams over. They have just four interceptions on the year (94th nationally) and are 48th in total turnovers forced at 11. Raiola has been prone to turnovers for his entire career dating back to Nebraska and will likely present a couple of opportunities -- either with interceptable balls or strip sacks -- for the Buckeyes to steal a possession or two. Ohio State has to capitalize on those chances if they want to help their sputtering offense. On the other side, the best way to make Ohio State tight in this one would be to pick off the young quarterback and make Ryan Day a bit anxious about letting the young man sling it. Oregon has nine interceptions this season (13th in the country), and if they can bait the freshman into an early mistake, it could alter the Buckeyes' game plan and give the Ducks an even better opportunity on the road. Ohio State vs. Oregon prediction, picks The Ducks have to pick up where they left off offensively to have a chance here, and they should push the tempo a bit and try to stretch things out in the air. Ohio State should be able to run the ball well, and at home I would expect Fahey and the offense to operate a bit better in the red zone to put touchdowns on the board when they do move the ball. A Ducks offense trying to push it in the passing game should result in big plays (possibly for both teams), and this is a rare big game where I'm anticipating plenty of points. And, as it’s been for most of the year, expect Jeremiah Smith to receive most of the targets on offense -- although it seems pretty clear that the Buckeyes could benefit from spreading the ball around a little more to keep defenses honest. Having said that, dropping a third regular-season game this Saturday against Oregon would no doubt shrink the Buckeyes’ playoff chances dramatically Luckily for Ohio State, Oregon’s season hasn’t turned out as expected either, after starting off as the No. 2-ranked team in the land, one spot behind the Buckeyes. away.headline: Ohio State football's Jay Timmons trending toward return against Oregon
away.blurb: Timmons, who was held out of last week’s loss at USC with an unspecified injury, was not included on the Buckeyes’ initial availability report released for their upcoming game against the Ducks. Timmons missed games against Iowa and Maryland earlier in October before returning at Indiana when he reaggravated his injury. He traveled with the Buckeyes to Los Angeles last week as he attempted to return but was ruled out near kickoff. Wide receivers Brock Boyd and Brandon Inniss were listed as questionable for Oregon after they were held out at USC. It was the second straight game Boyd was sidelined with an unspecified injury. Left tackle Ian Moore was also listed as questionable. Moore made a late exit against the Trojans as Austin Siereveld moved over from right tackle to replace him in the fourth quarter. Defensive tackle Eddrick Houston was not listed after he went down late last week and later limped off the field at the Coliseum, indicating he could be available against Oregon. He has also practiced in recent days, prompting coach Ryan Day to express optimism about his status on Nov. 4. “We’ll have to see how the next 48 hours go,” Day said, “but he’s had two good days of practice. That would really inject a lot for us in the back end.” The Buckeyes’ secondary felt the absence of Timmons against the Trojans as they surrendered their longest passes this season between a 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage and another 70-yard reception in the third quarter. The Oregon fans once sitting in the upper northeast corner of Ohio Stadium had made their way down to field level, filling in the bleachers Ohio State fans once occupied. Kentucky are ranked as high as it ever has, while the 6-2 Volunteers had their CFP hopes take a hit last week with a 27-24 loss at South Carolina . Now they will face Tennessee, Florida and Missouri in successive weeks, so Stein's crew will need to be on top of its game. UK already has victories over ranked Texas A&M and LSU squads. It comes in off an easy 34-27 victory against Vanderbilt and had a bye last week, so it should be ready for this one. The Wildcats put up 376 yards last week, including 173 on the ground, and allowed 247. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has been avoiding mistakes as UK relies on running backs CJ Baxter , Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. Minchey is completing 69% of his passes for 1,755 yards, 14 TDs and just one interception. He also has two rushing scores, but the running back trio is the bread and butter. All three backs average more than 5 yards per carry, with Baxter the bell cow, as he has 487 rushing yards and eight TDs. Patterson has 443 yards and three scores and Barnes has 224 and a TD on 43 carries. Baxter and Patterson each have runs of more than 70 yards. Both teams average more than 32 points per game and Tennessee is eighth in the SEC in total yardage (394.5 ypg) while UK is ninth (386.4). The Vols are much better defensively, ranking fourth in the conference in yards allowed (288.4 ypg) and third in scoring (16.3 ppg). The Wildcats are allowing 24.8 points (10th in SEC) and 362.6 yards per game (11th). Where Kentucky has a big edge is in turnover margin, as the Wildcats are plus-13, fourth-best in the nation, while the Vols are plus-3. The Volunteers are strong defensively, and their offense also relies heavily on the run game. Only South Carolina averages more rushing yards than the Vols' 213 yards per game among conference foes, while UK averages 167 per contest on the ground, seventh in the conference. Running back DeSean Bishop is sixth in the nation with 957 rushing yards and has four consecutive games over 100, including 220 against Auburn . He has also scored 11 touchdowns. Backup Daune Morris has 349 yards and two scores, and he and Bishop both average more than 5.5 yards per carry. Quarterback George MacIntyre has played in place of Faizon Brandon the past four games, but he has two TD passes and five interceptions over that span. He also made a costly mistake against the Gamecocks last week. He did have some big plays nullified and is completing 67% of his passes compared to Brandon's 60%, but the latter has accounted for 10 TDs. Brandon has just one interception but has been sacked 15 times. Both could see time, but Brandon has dealt with a shoulder injury and MacIntyre has been up and down, so the running game and defense will be the keys. The Vols lead FBS in sacks with 35, led by Tyree Weathersby's seven, which ties him for ninth in the nation. Xavier Gilliam has six and Mariyon Dye has five as they're among nine players with at least two. The Vols have turned the ball over a lot but have 14 takeaways, tied for 14th in FBS. The Wildcats are tied for fourth in the nation with 18. The hosts will be looking to make up for last week, when they rushed for 184 yards but MacIntyre fumbled on a strip sack with 33 seconds left to set up the winning field goal. He threw for 136 yards. The Vols had five sacks of LaNorris Sellers and controlled the ball but couldn't hold off the South Carolina rally. Kentucky has covered the spread in every game except the loss to Alabama, and its games have gone Over the total in five of eight, including two of three on the road. Six of eight Vols games have gone Under, with all five home games falling short of the total. They are 4-4 against the spread and 3-2 ATS in Knoxville. The Wildcats battled to a 21-17 victory against a comparable defense in Oklahoma , which is fifth in the SEC in total defense. Pictured: Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop Ryan Minion · Action Network Sat, November 7, 2026 at 9:58 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kentucky Wildcats take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Despite entering Saturday's Week 10 clash with a 7-1 overall record on the season, Kentucky remains a 6.5-point road underdog with a +188 price tag to pull off the outright upset. Tennessee is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -220. Kentucky is a 5.5-point underdog with a moneyline of +184. The total is set at 49.5 points (-110 / -110). Here's my Kentucky vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 7. Kentucky vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (-225) My Tennessee vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page , and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Tennessee Odds, Betting Line, Point Spread Kentucky vs Tennessee Spread : Kentucky +6, Tennessee -6 Kentucky vs Tennessee Over/Under : 49.5 Total Points Kentucky vs Tennessee Moneyline : Kentucky ML +170, Tennessee ML -205 In one of the bigger surprises of this college football season, the Wildcats have emerged as one of the best teams in the entire country in head coach Will Stein's first year at the helm. Kentucky senior QB Kenny Minchey has been phenomenal in his first season in Lexington after spending three years at Notre Dame and throwing the ball only 30 times there. Minchey has thrown for 1755 yards and 14 touchdowns over the Wildcats' first eight games this season with just one turnover. Freshman WR Kenny Darby has been Minchey's favorite target with over 500 yards and three touchdowns. Stein's rushing attack has been effective too, with senior tailback CJ Baxter rushing for nearly 500 yards and eight touchdowns. The Wildcat offense is averaging just shy of 33 points per game this season, but will get its most difficult test on Saturday against an elite Tennessee pass rush. Kentucky's defense has thrived under defensive coordinator Jay Bateman, who has built an aggressive, havoc -creating unit that has fared well against some elite SEC offenses this season. The Wildcats lead the SEC in interceptions and pass breakups, boasting an elite secondary led by veteran safeties Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell. While its front seven struggled early this season, Kentucky has improved drastically in the trenches over the course of the season. The 8th-ranked Wildcats are in a great spot to potentially qualify for the playoffs, but still must face several difficult conference opponents, starting with the Vols in Week 10. The 16th-ranked Volunteers put their postseason hopes on the line as Josh Heupel's bunch looks to evade a third loss this season that would very likely ruin their playoff resume. After a very promising 6-1 start to the season despite an ongoing QB battle between George MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon , Tennessee was defeated on the road at South Carolina this past weekend for the Vols' second loss of the year. Now they face a must-win game, with lingering questions about whether Heupel will stick with MacIntyre under center or return to top-ranked freshman QB Brandon. Regardless, betting markets have made their stance quite clear, with Tennessee currently listed as a near-touchdown favorite despite the Wildcats' breakout 7-1 campaign. While WR Mike Matthews has recorded over 500 receiving yards this season, Tennessee has relied far more on its rushing attack, with tailback DeSean Bishop rushing for 957 yards and 11 touchdowns, ranking sixth and ninth in all of college football, respectively. However, the Vols' defense has thrived all year, particularly at home, where it allows SEC opponents the third-fewest PPG in the conference (16.25). Jim Knowles was brought in as defensive coordinator this past offseason after serving in the same capacity for Penn State , and has significantly improved a unit that fell to 81st in the country in EPA (Expected Points Added) last season. Tennessee's defense boasts an elite linebacker corps ranked in the top 10 nationally, featuring Edwin Spillman, Amare Campbell, Arion Carter, and Jeremiah Telander. While the Vols' defense has carried this team for most of the season, especially at home in Knoxville, their offense will need to show up in this matchup, given how impressive Michey has been at avoiding turnovers. I expect this to be one of the best matchups in an absolutely loaded Week 10 slate. While I have been very impressed with the Wildcats offense and a much-improved defensive unit, I expect the atmosphere to be quite chaotic given how difficult it is for SEC foes to escape Neyland Stadium in Knoxville with an outright victory. The Vols boast an extremely dominant pass rush that should give Kentucky's offensive line fits considering how much that unit has struggled to contain elite edge pressure. That said, I feel betting markets are giving Tennessee a tad too much credit given their fragile situation at QB. In what I expect to be a pretty closely contested matchup, I'm going with the Volunteers moneyline. I got it at -210 earlier this week as soon as the line opened, and while I typically don't lay that much juice on a moneyline, especially considering the volatility of betting college football, I have confidence Tennessee gets the outright win, but laying close to a touchdown versus a red-hot Wildcat bunch is far from ideal. Though Tennessee's moneyline has since crept up to -230, I still don't mind playing the Vols at that number. Pete Fiutak · College Football News Fri, November 6, 2026 at 9:25 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky is No. 6 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and Tennessee is No. 13. On any other Saturday, and in any other time slot, this would be the biggest game of the day, with huge SEC and CFP implications. This starts an hour before it's on, but by the second quarter, Georgia-Ole Miss and Miami-Notre Dame will both be ramping up while the Cats and Vols are humming. This will still earn a front-and-center spot, though. As good as Tennessee has been – including a relatively dominant 26-10 win over Alabama – it's coming off a 27-24 loss to South Carolina, and it's one loss away from being in a really, really tough spot to stay alive for the CFP. Kentucky got destroyed by Alabama in Week 2, but it's on a six-game winning streak. It pulled off great 35-34 wins over both LSU and South Carolina, and it won at Oklahoma. It has breathing room with just one loss, but with a rough finishing kick, beating Tennessee would be gigantic. Kentucky vs Tennessee: Quick Hits Tennessee has just one home game left after this, hosting LSU between road games at Texas A&M and Vanderbilt. Kentucky gets two of its last three games at home, hosting Florida next week and with Louisville to close, going to Missouri in between those two. Tennessee has won the last five meetings, going back to a 34-7 UK win in 2020. How To Watch Kentucky vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 6:15 PM ET TV: ESPN Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Kentucky Will Win No, Kentucky isn't as talented as most of the top SEC teams, and yeah, there are a whole lot of things wrong that need tweaking. But this Wildcat team just doesn't give anyone anything to work with. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and No. 1 in turnover margin. The Wildcats have only been hit with 15 penalties over the last five weeks, and they haven't turned it over in any of the last four games. On the flip side, Tennessee gets flagged an average of 7.6 times per game, and while turnovers aren't a big problem, it gave the ball away eight times over the last four games. Why Tennessee Will Win Tennessee has to keep the mistakes to a minimum, and it has to keep the offense moving. It doesn't have to take any big chances against a Kentucky defense that's good against the run but doesn't do much to come up with third down stops. The Volunteer pass rush is the best in the nation, and it should be disruptive in the Kentucky backfield, but it really is about the offense. Tennessee's ground game has been fantastic – it's 16th in the nation – and that's a jumping-off point. Kentucky vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines The Vols are 6-0 when the offense generates more than 320 total yards, and 0-2 when it doesn't. Only Vanderbilt and Youngstown State failed to get at least 340 yards against the Kentucky defense. Yes, Kentucky is for real. It's well coached, sharp as a tack, and it's one of those teams that just knows how to win. But with two weeks off after the South Carolina loss, the rejuvenated Vols will make a massive statement in both the SEC and College Football Playoff chases with a strong performance. picks.blurb: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Knoxville News Sentinel · The Tennessean Sat, November 7, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Tennessee football opens a November to either remember or forget with a top-15 matchup against Kentucky on Nov. 7 at Neyland Stadium The Vols (6-2, 3-2 SEC) lost at South Carolina two weeks ago on a last-second field goal, earning a second SEC loss before the final month of the season. Kentucky (7-1, 5-1) is also coming off of an open date and has a clear path to the SEC Championship Game and the CFP. First-year coach Will Stein has molded his roster into a team that limits its mistakes and maximizes other teams' turnovers. UK has beaten Tennessee in Knoxville once since 1984, the 2020 win in front of a COVID-limited crowd at Neyland. Here are Knox News' staff predictions for Tennessee-Kentucky: Tennessee-Kentucky expert predictions Adam Sparks, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 28, Kentucky 24 The Vols can certainly beat themselves against the most disciplined team in the SEC. Kentucky leads the league in turnover margin and fewest penalties. But UT can take control of this game by winning the line of scrimmage. That means DeSean Bishop earns bruising yards and UT's defensive line collapses the pocket around Kenny Minchey. Give Tennessee the edge because of the overwhelming atmosphere of Neyland Stadium in a night game in dark mode. Emmett Siegel, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 24, Kentucky 20 The Vols still have to find something in their passing game , which is statistically the worst in the SEC. Even if that doesn't come to fruition, though, Tennessee's rushing attack and defense have been good enough to beat the toughest teams on its schedule. Perhaps the open week helped Tennessee clean up some of last game's mistakes before playing a team that doesn't make many. Playing at home could push it over the top. Cora Hall, UT beat reporter: Kentucky 27, Tennessee 24 Both teams are had a week off and are rested going into this matchup, and the Wildcats have proven they can will their way to a win when it matters. The Vols will get close, but they've been too inconsistent to bet on a win here. Stephen Thompson, UT beat reporter: Tennessee 17, Kentucky 13 I've surrendered to the idea that George MacIntyre is who he is, at least for now. But Tennessee's defense is as good as any in the country and the Neyland effect will be a difference maker in another ugly, but tight win for the Vols. Wynton Jackson, sports reporter: Tennessee 26, Kentucky 21 The Vols likely need to be perfect throughout the rest of the season to reach the College Football Playoff. Coming off the bye, that road starts with an unexpected matchup against No. 7 Kentucky. The Wildcats have solid wins, but a trip to Neyland with a national spotlight brings heightened pressure. John Adams, columnist: Tennessee 27, Kentucky 20 The Wildcats have a better record and a higher national ranking than the Vols. Moreover, Kentucky is clearly headed in the right direction under first-year coach Will Stein. But history tells us that Tennessee is always the wrong direction for Kentucky football, which has lost 38 of the previous 41 games in the series. Gentry Estes, Tennessean columnist: Tennessee 23, Kentucky 14 Props to the Wildcats on a great season, but it just feels like they are due for a letdown in a tough rivalry road game. Neyland should be jumping for this one. This article originally appeared on Knoxville News Sentinel: Tennessee football vs Kentucky picks: Vols don't lose to Wildcats in Knoxville, right?

picks.headline: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 6, 2026 at 6:30 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to a hostile Neyland Stadium to take on the Tennessee Volunteers at 6:15 P.M. ET on Saturday night. This is a massive game with a lot at stake for both teams, the Wildcats are undefeated on the road this season and they will try to continue that streak in this game. We laid out the path to victory for Kentucky and the key areas they need to win to improve to 8-1 on the season. It is time to give some final thoughts on the matchup and give a game prediction. As I stated earlier in the week on my Tennessee defense preview , but I truly think this game comes down to Will Stein's offense versus Jim Knowles' defense. They have met three times and Coach Stein has gotten the best of Knowles in two of those three meetings. Kentucky has to continue to play efficient on offense and play clean. I think they have a great opportunity to methodically move the football down the field as they have all season against this defense. This game starts and ends in the trenches, on both sides of the football. Tennessee's defensive line is the strength of their team, but Kentucky's offensive line is playing better than any offensive line in the country. They have to stabilize defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam, who has been wrecking offensive gameplans all season long. A key matchup to watch is Kentucky center Coleton Price against Gilliam, Price has been one of the best centers in the country and he will have his hands full in this game. Kentucky has to win this game on the line of scrimmage, and I have confidence in the Wildcats offensive line to gain the edge in that matchup. Tennessee's offensive line has been above average as run blockers, but they do struggle in pass protection. Kentucky forcing Tennessee into a dropback heavy game script could be critical, but they have to stop the run in order to do that. Kentucky's defensive line has gotten consistent pressure all season, and I am very intrigued to see how this defensive line gets after a pocket passer like George MacIntyre because they have faced a mobile quarterback in every game this season. Kentucky has to win the line of scrimmage, and this is the best offensive line the Vols have faced this season. I think the Wildcats defensive line has been underrated this year, and they can make a statement on Saturday. The run defense has improved tremendously in the month of October, and slowing down the Vols heavy rushing attack is crucial. If they can force Tennessee into a heavy dropback game, Kentucky will be able to create turnovers like they have all season. Truthfully, I believe the biggest advantage is Kentucky's coaching staff getting two weeks to prepare for this football game. Tennessee is coming off the bye week as well, but Josh Heupel and Jim Knowles are going to do what they do. Kentucky's coaching staff has added plenty of wrinkles week-to-week, so I can only imagine what they will have in store with two weeks to prepare. This is an advantage for Kentucky, particularly on the offensive side of the football. We all know this history of this series, it has not been kind to Kentucky. However, this is a different era of college football and Kentucky football. If you remove the history and helmet logos, I think Kentucky has the advantage at quarterback and offensive line as well as a hotshot head coach that has done an unthinkable turnaround in year one for this program. It will be a close game in the fourth quarter, and how could you not trust Will Stein and Kenny Minchey under those circumstances. Prediction: Kentucky 24, Tennessee 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky at Tennessee: Final thoughts and prediction

picks.blurb: Rece Davis Predicts Notre Dame Playoff Problem Ahead of Top-5 Miami Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Notre Dame could find itself in the same College Football Playoff predicament that ended its 2025 season if it can’t beat No. 1 Miami on Saturday, according to ESPN College GameDay host Rece Davis. Davis made the case on ESPN’s College GameDay Podcast with co-hosts Pete Thamel and Dan Wetzel, saying the No. 4 Fighting Irish (7-1) would be in “ very much the same situation as a year ago ” with a loss. Rece Davis on Notre Dame’s resume Notre Dame Fighting Irish head coach Marcus Freeman reacts during the first half against the Brigham Young Cougars | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis noted that ESPN’s Football Power Index, a forward-looking measure, ranks Notre Dame No. 1. Miami, however, ranks No. 1 in strength of record, which grades what a team has done against its schedule. Davis said that split will shape the debate over the Irish. He expects them to stay in the field unless the Hurricanes blow them out, but he doesn’t see the questions about their resume going away. “I think Notre Dame will still be OK absent getting run out of the stadium, which I cannot conceive of happening,” Davis said. “So it’s going to be a little bit different than last year, but the argument, the discussion, is going to be the same if they don’t win this game.” He added: “When you get down to who did you play and who did you beat, especially the who did you beat portion of who did you play, they won’t have much on the paper.” Why does Notre Dame’s schedule matter? General view as Brigham Young Cougars fans celebrate on the field after the game against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Notre Dame has faced one team ranked at the time of kickoff this season, and it lost 28-24 at BYU on Oct. 17. None of its seven wins came against a team in this week’s AP Top 25. The Irish beat Wisconsin, Rice, Michigan State, Purdue, North Carolina, Stanford and Navy. After Miami, they close with Boston College, SMU and Syracuse, who are a combined 14-10 and unranked. Notre Dame does carry a protection it lacked last year. The College Football Playoff guarantees the Irish a spot if they finish in the top 12 of the final rankings. A loss to Miami would test that cushion, though, because Notre Dame would sit at 7-2 with no win over a ranked opponent and no ranked teams left on its schedule. picks.blurb: Colin Cowherd Predicts National Championship Rematch After Notre Dame Win Over Miami Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS Fox Sports host Colin Cowherd is sticking with Notre Dame and Miami as his national championship pairing after the Fighting Irish handed the top-ranked Hurricanes their first loss of the season, 31-24, Saturday night in South Bend. “Nothing I saw last night changes that opinion ,” Cowherd wrote on X on Sunday morning, adding that he said before the season the two programs “would meet for the natty” and that “only Georgia is close.” Why is Cowherd still riding with Notre Dame? Fans are seen on the field after Notre Dame Fighting Irish defeated the Miami Hurricanes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Cowherd backed the Irish before they played a snap. “I picked Notre Dame to win the whole thing. They’re going to be my national champion ,” he said in late August. Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr held up his end of that pick Saturday, completing 29 of 40 passes for 319 yards and three touchdowns. He hit Micah Gilbert for two scores and Jordan Faison for another as the Irish built a 24-3 lead early in the third quarter. Miami pulled within a touchdown, but Notre Dame safety Luke Talich intercepted Miami quarterback Darian Mensah late in the third quarter and later broke up a potential tying touchdown pass to tight end Elija Lofton. The win mattered most for an Irish team that entered with the No. 11 College Football Playoff ranking that surprised ESPN’s Kirk Herbstreit. Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman called it “ as special of a moment , as special of an outcome that I’ve been a part of since I’ve been the head coach here.” The Irish close the regular season against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. Malachi Toney and a Miami rematch Miami (FL) Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) celebrates with tight end Gavin Mueller (87) after scoring a touchdown | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Cowherd attached one condition to his title game pick. “I would take the Canes in a rematch if Malachi Toney plays,” he wrote. Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice Wednesday and had tightrope surgery Thursday. The sophomore led the ACC with 73 catches, 1,027 receiving yards and 13 touchdowns through eight games, and CBS Sports reported he’s expected to miss four to six weeks . That timeline could put Toney back for the ACC Championship Game on Dec. 5 and keeps him on track for the playoff. His absence showed in a first half that ended with Miami trailing 17-3. Mensah then threw three second-half touchdown passes, two of them to Duke transfer Cooper Barkate. Miami finishes the regular season with home games against Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College. Georgia rolls Ole Miss in Oxford Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart reacts during the second half against the Mississippi Rebels | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. The second-ranked Bulldogs backed up Cowherd’s lone exception Saturday, routing Ole Miss 42-7 as Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another. Georgia led 28-0 at halftime, rushed for 295 yards and snapped Ole Miss’ 16-game home winning streak . The win was Georgia head coach Kirby Smart’s first at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and it came days after former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer named Georgia the best team in college football . The selection committee releases its second College Football Playoff rankings Tuesday at approximately 9 p.m. ET on ESPN, and Georgia has a strong case to replace Miami at No. 1. Miami vs Notre Dame predictions for Week 10 ⭐Spread prediction Over/Under prediction Prop prediction Miami TT Over 23.5 TOP PICK Who will win Miami vs Notre Dame today: Miami +7.5 The news that Malachi Toney was injured in practice this week and won't play against Notre Dame has dominated headlines and shifted the Fighting Irish from 5.5-point favorites to 7.5-point favorites. But even without Toney, I like Miami to cover +6.5 or better on the road. Darian Mensah is among the Heisman Trophy favorites for a reason; he leads the country in QBR (90.3) and adjusted completion percentage (86.2%). He also has one of the best running back duos in college football and a No. 2 wide receiver in Cooper Barkate , whom he trusts immensely. Mensah won the ACC Championship at Duke last year with Barkate as his top receiver (1,106 receiving yards). Even without Toney, Miami has more talented playmakers than CJ Carr and Notre Dame, and the Irish aren't healthy in their back seven. Notre Dame has ruled out linebacker Drayk Bowen, safety Tae Johnson, and cornerback DJ McKinney. Miami vs Notre Dame Over/Under pick: Over 54.5 With Mensah and Carr arguably the top two QBs in college football this season, I would play the Over at 55.5 or better , even with Toney out. Mensah is deadly accurate and ranks No. 1 in college football in TD passes (25), with Miami ranking No. 2 in the country in offensive success rate (52.4%). Notre Dame isn't far behind, though, sitting No. 4 in offensive success rate (51.4%) thanks to Carr, who r anks eighth in QBR (82.6), 11th in big-time throw rate (6.9%), and 18th in TD passes (18). Miami's pass defense has also been suspect at times, and Carr can take advantage. The Hurricanes are ranked just 110th in EPA per dropback. In the Fighting Irish's previous two games against teams ranked in the Top 50 by SP+ , they hit the Over. Miami vs Notre Dame prop: Miami TT Over 23.5 Toney is one of the best wide receivers in recent college football history, but Miami's offense has been a force with Mensah at QB and Dawson calling plays, and I don't think it will just collapse without its top receiver. I like the Hurricanes to hit the Over on their team total at 23.5 or better against a Notre Dame defense that allowed 28 points to BYU without its best offensive player, LJ Martin . Miami's passing attack is far more prolific than BYU's, with Miami's offense leading the country in EPA per dropback and net adjusted EPA per play. Notre Dame's defense has also been shaky on money downs this season, ranking 67th nationally in third/fourth down success rate (43.6%). Miami vs Notre Dame combo This is the "game of the century" of the week in college football and the No. 1 must-watch matchup in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , featuring the season's most loaded slate. While Miami would certainly be an upset threat to Notre Dame with Toney, I don't think Mario Cristobal's team will roll over in its biggest game of the season. The Hurricanes ended last season by covering the spread in four straight College Football Playoff games , including three as an underdog. Cristobal knows how to get his team up, and Notre Dame has had slow starts in three of its last four games, failing to cover in all three of those games as a favorite . Photo By - Reuters Connect. Darian Mensah, CJ Carr, NCAAF. South Bend will be the epicenter of the college football universe on Saturday night when the top-ranked Miami Hurricanes roll into town to face the Notre Dame Fighting Irish. We won't get to see Malachi Toney in action, but our Miami vs. Notre Dame prop picks for this heavyweight bout focus on the showdown between elite quarterbacks Darian Mensah and CJ Carr. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Miami vs. Notre Dame predictions ahead of kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. Best Miami vs Notre Dame props Prop pick #1: CJ Carr Over 4.5 rush attempts I gave out this same prop when Notre Dame faced BYU, and CJ Carr came through. I'm backing it again, up to 55%, for many of the same reasons. It starts with the game plan. This Miami defense ranks second in EPA per rush but 110th in EPA per pass. That means we'll likely see fewer handoffs and more dropback opportunities. That also puts Carr up against a Hurricanes front that ranks 15th in pass-rush grade, per PFF, and 29th nationally in sack rate. Carr has shown this season that he's not afraid to scramble. Factor in sacks counting as rush attempts, and he should clear this total for the fifth time in seven contests. Prop pick #2: Micah Gilbert Over 31.5 receiving yards Jordan Faison leads all Notre Dame receivers with 56 targets, while Jaden Greathouse and Micah Gilbert are tied with 33 targets apiece. But Gilbert is the player being undervalued here, and I'm backing him up to 54%. Miami's secondary isn't just struggling in coverage; it's also struggling to make tackles in the open field. Gilbert has the best yards after catch per reception (5.5) of Carr's top three targets and ranks second behind Faison in yards per route run. Gilbert is also the most reliable of the three, securing 72.7% of his targets. He's averaging 70.4 receiving yards in the six games in which he's run at least 20 routes. He's a bargain with a receiving yards line that's less than half of Faison's 69.5-yard total. Prop pick #3: Darian Mensah Over 1.5 passing touchdowns With Malachi Toney sidelined, Darian Mensah has an opportunity to take another step toward the Heisman tonight, and I'm backing him up to 55% to throw multiple touchdown passes. Not only do the Hurricanes rank third in red-zone scoring, but only Notre Dame has a higher offensive Eckel rate than Miami this season. As well as Notre Dame defends, the Irish are depleted on the back end heading into this game. Defensive captain Drayk Bowen is out at linebacker, and the secondary will be without DJ McKinney and Tae Johnson. The Irish gave up three touchdown passes to UNC's Billy Edwards, one of the few quality passers they've faced this season. Mensah leads the nation in passing efficiency and completion rate, and getting him at this number is a gift. Our Miami vs. Notre Dame score prediction backs the Fighting Irish to avenge last year's 27-24 loss and hand the Hurricanes their first defeat of the season. No. 1 Miami (8-0) visits No. 11 Notre Dame (7-1) tonight at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend, Ind., with kickoff set for 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Our AI projection model forecasts a 35-29 Notre Dame win as part of our college football AI predictions for Week 10 , putting us on Miami +7.5 and Over 54.5. Miami vs Notre Dame AI prediction Miami's Marquise Lightfoot has seven sacks. Notre Dame has allowed two all season. The Irish can afford to trust CJ Carr on passing downs, even against a front that gives up just 69.8 rushing yards per game. Carr has thrown 18 touchdown passes against one interception. Miami has allowed 10 touchdown passes in its last three games alone. If Lightfoot can't get home with a four-man rush, the Hurricanes have a tough choice between giving Carr time or sending a blitzer and leaving one fewer defender in coverage. That matchup gives the Irish the advantage outright. Cooper Barkate gives Darian Mensah a familiar option on third down. Barkate had 1,106 receiving yards at Duke last season with Mensah as his quarterback. Now they face a Notre Dame secondary missing cornerback DJ McKinney and safety Brauntae Johnson. The Irish are also without linebacker Drayk Bowen against Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory, who have each rushed for more than 450 yards. That gives Miami a way to sustain drives while it replaces Malachi Toney's catches. Rob Paul also likes the underdog in his Miami vs. Notre Dame prediction . With temperatures around 40 degrees and light winds forecast at kickoff, Miami's red-zone possessions matter more to our total pick than the weather. away.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. home.headline: Miami gets concerning Malachi Toney injury update ahead of Notre Dame clash
home.blurb: Miami will undoubtedly want Toney available for this crucial matchup, but playing through an ankle injury could bring risks for one of the Hurricanes’ most valuable offensive weapons. The undefeated Miami Hurricanes face a major test this weekend when they battle the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in a showdown between College Football Playoff contenders. Miami enters the matchup ranked No. 1 in both the AP Top 25 poll and the initial CFP rankings. Much of that has been thanks to the on-field brilliance of quarterback Darian Mensah and star wide receiver Malachi Toney. However, a concerning injury update regarding Toney surfaced on Wednesday, potentially putting his availability for the Notre Dame matchup in jeopardy. According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel , sources told him and Max Olson that the Hurricanes’ Toney is dealing with an ankle injury, leaving his status for Saturday’s matchup “uncertain.” “Toney is expected to press and attempt to play, given the magnitude of the game,” Thamel also said in his X report. More news: CFP Committee Chair Under Fire for Alabama’s Controversial Ranking Toney ranks second in NCAA football with 73 receptions, third with 1,027 receiving yards, and third with 13 touchdowns. The 5-foot-11 sophomore has delivered several impressive performances this past season, including 154 yards and two touchdowns in Miami’s double-overtime win over Florida State. As of this writing, Toney is also considered one of the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. Mensah has emerged as the favorite to win, and Toney’s production has played a significant role in the quarterback’s success this season. Saturday’s game carries major CFP implications for Miami and Notre Dame. Both teams appeared in the initial CFP rankings, with Miami holding the top spot and Notre Dame landing at No. 11. However, several games remain on their schedules before the playoff field is finalized. A loss could seriously damage Notre Dame’s chances of getting into the College Football Playoff. Meanwhile, Miami is undefeated, and a loss could hurt its standing in the CFP rankings. Keeping that perfect record could strengthen Miami’s chances of a first-round bye in the CFP. The Miami Hurricanes take on the Notre Dame Fighting Irish at 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Nov. 7. home.blurb: Which made it all the more gut-wrenching when the Heisman Trophy front-runner came down with an injury during practice the week leading up to the Hurricanes ' mammoth matchup against Notre Dame . Reports said Toney suffered a high ankle sprain on Wednesday, Nov. 4, and that he would undergo surgery, putting not only the showdown with the No. 6 Fighting Irish out of the question, but the rest of his stellar season in jeopardy. Toney has battled injuries throughout the season, briefly leaving games against Wake Forest on Sept. 18, Clemson on Oct. 3, Florida State on Oct. 17 and Pittsburgh on Oct. 24. He never went back to the locker room, though his limited play late against Wake can be explicitly tied to the offense's stagnation and one of their closest games of the season. And he was able to shake off his injury vs. Pitt en route to breaking his own Miami record with 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns. When will Malachi Toney return? According to the Cleveland Clinic , high ankle sprains occur when the ligaments that attach the tibia to the fibula near the foot are torn or damaged. Recovery takes six to eight weeks, though the Clinic says it might take longer for athletes to return to play. However, there is hope Toney can return sooner, with initial reports indicating he could return in time for the College Football Playoff. The first round of the CFP is Dec. 18-19, six weeks away. If Miami retains one of the top four spots in the final CFP rankings (they're No. 1 heading into today's game at Notre Dame), they would first play in the quarterfinals Dec. 30 or Jan. 1, in about eight weeks. There's a chance Toney could return for the ACC championship game Dec. 5, four weeks from now. Our Staff Picks and Final Scores Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS No. 10 Ole Miss (6-2, 4-2) and No. 2 Georgia (7-1, 5-1) are set to square off on Saturday , in what will mark one of the biggest and most consequential games in the history of Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. In order to maintain control of its College Football Playoff destiny, Ole Miss will have to knock off Georgia for the third time in the program’s last four matchups. With a loss, the Rebels will put their season resume in the hands of the playoff committee with little optimism of returning to meaningful postseason play. Considering what Ole Miss has left in the final quarter of its season, there would be a lot of ground to make up. Ahead of the Rebels' top-10 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss Rebels On SI Staff Predictions Oct 18, 2025; Athens, Georgia, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) runs the ball for a touchdown against Mississippi Rebels defensive tackle Will Echoles (52) during the first half of the game at Sanford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Matt Galatzan Matt Galatzan The last two times these two teams met, both games were absolute cinema. Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels offense was unstoppable in both matchups, particularly in Round 2, when they knocked of the Bulldogs in the College Football Playoff. This year, the calculus has changed a bit. The Rebels have a new play caller, and new weapons on the outside. The Defense has also been struggling as of late. On the other side, the Bulldogs are built on defense, running the football and controlling the clock - exactly where Ole Miss has been exploited defensively. For Ole Miss to win here, I think Chambliss - especially without Kewan Lacy in the lineup - is going to have to be Superman. We have seen him do it before plenty of times, but if the Bulldogs can deploy a similar game plan that Texas did two weeks ago, it could be a long day. Shekai Mills-Knight could be an X-factor, but it's hard to be able to rely on a redshirt freshman on a stage like this. The Rebels do have an elite home field advantage, but at the end of the day, I think it all comes down to the Rebels defense and if they can hold up against the Georgia run game. I'll take the Dawgs in a tight one. Georgia 31, Ole Miss 27 Understandably, almost everyone had the LSU game circled on Ole Miss’ schedule going into the season. September and October couldn’t have looked any different for Ole Miss, particularly on the defensive side of the ball. Offensively, Trinidad Chambliss will need to play a game similar to the one he played against LSU all the way back in Week 3. Without Kewan Lacy, Ole Miss will need efficiency from Chambliss, Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight on the ground. That should translate into a motivated team and an electric environment in Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, and when playing in The Vaught, especially at night, there isn’t a team in the country I’d take over Ole Miss. The Rebels are 26-1 at home since 2023, including a victory over the Bulldogs in the 2024 regular season that had very similar stakes as this game. Picking any team, let alone one that’s been as hot and cold as Ole Miss has been at times this season, to beat the No. 2 team in the country could age poorly. Despite that, give me Pete Golding, Trinidad Chambliss and the rest of the Ole Miss Rebels to win and keep their playoff and SEC Championship ambitions alive and send the Rebel fans home happy on Saturday night. The Bulldogs average 200 rushing yards per game, and if Ole Miss can’t stop it, the Rebels could struggle to pull ahead. Golding will need Trinidad Chambliss to deliver if Ole Miss is going to defeat Georgia. If the Rebels consistently get off the field on third down and establish their offensive rhythm, I think Ole Miss gets a huge win. Trinidad Chambliss is beginning to look like himself again, and with the Rebels offensive line performing about as good as ever before, I expect an incredible offensive showing from the home side. Kirby Smart’s side will never go down easy, and Gunnar Stockton is a solid leader for the Bulldogs offense. Sparks will fly in Oxford, but a repeat of 2024 is in order. My Georgia vs. Ole Miss prediction and college football picks for tonight expect Kirby Smart's defense to rise to the occasion against Trinidad Chambliss & Co. as the Bulldogs seek revenge for last year's Sugar Bowl loss to the Rebels. Georgia is a 3.5-point favorite as it visits Vaught-Hemingway Stadium in Oxford, Miss., on Saturday, Nov. 7, while the total sits at 56.5. Don't miss kickoff at 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC. TOP PICK Who will win Georgia vs Ole Miss today: Georgia -3.5 Georgia and Ole Miss played two wild shootouts last year, with the Bulldogs winning the regular-season matchup and the Rebels taking it in the Sugar Bowl. This time around, I like Georgia to cover as many as 6.5 points on the road against Ole Miss. Defense will be the difference in the matchup this year, with Georgia having one of the best in the country ( ranked No. 2 by SP+ ), and Ole Miss' being one of the worst in the SEC. With the Rebels down All-American running back Kewan Lacy , the Bulldogs' defense can lock in on stopping Trinidad Chambliss . Chambliss has faced one other defense ranked top five by SP+, Texas , and struggled in a loss. Against the Longhorns, he threw three interceptions and put up a season-low 60% adjusted completion percentage. Georgia vs Ole Miss Over/Under pick: Under 56.5 Though both games between these teams last year were full of points, Georgia's defense should keep it relatively low-scoring this time around, and I would play the Under at 55.5 or better . The Bulldogs' defense ranks top 20 nationally in available yards percentage (33.5%) , havoc rate (19.4%), and success rate allowed (35.2%). With no Lacy for Ole Miss, it'll put even more on Chambliss, who has frequently had to carry the team this season, and we saw that approach fall flat against Texas. However, Georgia's offense hasn't been lighting up the scoreboard lately either, averaging just 23.6 points per game in its last three outings. So while this is one of the must-watch matchups in my Week 10 Top 25 predictions , it's not because I'm expecting another shootout. Georgia vs Ole Miss combo Ole Miss is a feast-or-famine type of team. The Rebels beat LSU and Missouri , but were blown out by Florida and fell behind so quickly against Texas that they couldn't dig themselves out. That's what happens when you lean so heavily on a star QB to make up for an inconsistent run game and one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Against Georgia, Chambliss won't be Superman; Smart has too much NFL talent on a defense that's allowed more than 20 points just once this season. If Ole Miss falls behind, Georgia's offense will lean on Gunner Stockton to manage the game and take a ball-control approach against a Rebels defense ranked 88th in the country in EPA per rush. Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Georgia team total Over 30.5 Georgia vs Ole Miss prop: Ole Miss team total Under 26.5 Chambliss can only do so much, and against a freakishly athletic and long Georgia defense, I don't think Ole Miss will be scoring at nearly as high a clip as it has against lesser SEC teams. I would take the Under on Ole Miss' team total at 24.5 or better . Georgia linebacker Chris Cole is arguably the best defensive player in the country, and Glenn Schumann and Kirby Smart could deploy him as a Chambliss stopper. With 4.5 40-yard dash speed and nearly 34-inch arms, Cole has earned his nickname of "Tarantula." Look for the Bulldogs to spy Chambliss with him and use him as a blitzer too; he leads Georgia in pressures (24) and pass-rush win rate (17.4%). With Cole hunting Chambliss and the Bulldogs' defense ranking top 20 in rush success rate (37.8%), Ole Miss will struggle to find the end zone. He unfortunately was hurt during the second game of Georgia's season and hasn't seen the field since. Earlier this week though he was marked probable to play on Georgia's official injury report and on Thursday he was nowhere to be found on their report which means he has been officially cleared to play. This injury update does need to be taken with a grain of salt. Nate Frazier came off Georgia's injury report heading into the Alabama game, but he still didn't play. There however is just as good of a chance that he won't be able to play either. Another injury report will come out Friday night before one final injury update about an hour before kickoff on Saturday. That can't be held against him though because the starters barely played in Georgia's season opener against Tennessee State before he got hurt the following week in Week 2. Canion has a lot of potential though that Georgia hasn't seen yet. Last year at Georgia Tech he was an integral part of their talented offense as he recorded 33 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns. He isn't a player that will ever be the No. 1 target in Georgia's offense, but he can be another reliable option for Gunner Stockton in a game where UGA needs a lot of offense. This is great timing for Georgia because the Ole Miss offense, with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, dominated UGA the two times they played last season. Georgia's offense likely needs to score a lot of points to win this game, and Canion being back on the field will help them accomplish that. home.blurb: Friday Ole Miss vs. Georgia Injury Report: Keaton Thomas Probable - The Rebel Walk Recent ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss linebacker Keaton Thomas is probable for Saturday night's game against No. 2 Georgia after being questionable on Thursday, according to the SEC's Friday availability report. Defensive end Kam Franklin remains questionable. The report was posted at 7:10 p.m. CT on Friday. Ole Miss' list of players who are out did not change, with running back Kewan Lacy and eight others ruled out again. Georgia, meanwhile, moved three players from questionable to out: inside linebacker AJ Kruah , safety Tyriq Green and defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye . Keaton Thomas moves up to probable Thomas, a linebacker, was questionable on both Wednesday and Thursday and is now probable for Saturday night. That is the only change to the Ole Miss availability designations from Thursday. Cornerback Jalyn Crawford and safety MJ Preston remain probable, and no other Rebels are listed. Kam Franklin remains questionable Franklin has carried the questionable tag all week and has not been cleared with kickoff about 23 hours away. He has 25 tackles, including 15 solo stops and 10 assists, along with 5.0 tackles for loss, two sacks, a pass breakup and a fumble recovery he returned for a touchdown through eight games this season. He was named a leader of the defense in our September feature on Franklin . Without him, Ole Miss would lose one of its best pass rushers and run stoppers against a Georgia offense that scores 41 points per game. Georgia's report got shorter on the questionable side and longer on the out side. Next up for Jon Sumrall and Co. are the Oklahoma Sooners, who travel to Ben Hill Griffin Stadium in Week 10 for the first-ever meeting between the two schools as mutual members of the Southeastern Confernece. They have met twice before — both times in the postseason — including the 2009 BCS Championship game, in which the Orange and Blue prevailed for their second national title in three years. This season, Florida (5-3, 3-3 SEC) sits just outside of the US LMB Coaches Poll top 25 and just barely hanging on in the AP Top 25 at No. 25, while Oklahoma arrives in Gainesville voteless in both major polls with a 4-4 record (2-3 SEC). Ahead of Florida's Week 10 SEC showdown in the Swamp, Gators Wire's staff convened to offer their expert predictions and picks for the matchup. Take a look below at what we had to say. If the Gators can clean up the turnovers and penalties that have plagued them, I think they can take control early and maintain a comfortable advantage throughout the second half. — David Rosenberg PREDICTION : Florida 28, Oklahoma 14 '(The Gators) will need a big offensive day and to limit turnovers' The Gators need a win to get back on track, and what better way than to face a program in Oklahoma that currently ranks in the SEC's bottom three in points per game. On the other hand, they are one of the conference's better defenses. While their offense has slipped a bit, the Gators have shown progress defensively, and I expect the trend to continue in Ben Hill Griffin. OU has struggled offensively throughout this season, and Florida's defense has been opportunistic in spurts. The Gators have been the better team throughout the season but have had multiple hiccups. To win this game, they will need a big offensive day and to limit turnovers, because this season's numbers show Oklahoma won't be able to keep up. — Michael Trim Jr. PREDICTION: Florida 28, Oklahoma 17 'I think the Gators' defense does enough to stifle Oklahoma' There shouldn't be any panic in Gainesville as the Gators are ahead of schedule in year one of the Jon Sumrall era, but that doesn't mean the early 4-0 start didn't get everyone's hopes up about this ideation of the Gators' roster. Florida showed the country what it was capable of during that first month of the season but reminded the college football world it had a long way to go in order to consistently compete with top programs like Georgia. The key on Saturday is to steady a ship that has been battered with turmoil in the last month. Jadan Baugh and the UF rushing attack have taken a giant step back, several skill position players have been in and out of the lineup and the quarterback now feels extremely uncertain. After Philo's nighmareish first half against Georgia, I anticipate Sumrall will run both he and Tramell Jones Jr. for the OU game. Whoever has the hot hand or creates the most favorable matchup will get the majority of the snaps. Ball security will be the biggest factor for whoever stays on the field, as four turnovers proved costly. Saturday should be a chance for the Gators' defense to shine. The Sooners need to win two of their final four to earn bowl eligibility . With a new voice leading the offense, the Sooners are hoping for a turnaround to end the 2026 season. Jason Witten takes over an offense that has underachieved this season, given the number of returning starters along the offensive line and the weapons at returning quarterback John Mateer. How much better can Oklahoma be in a week is the question on everyone's minds. It's unlikely the Sooners will suddenly erupt on offense, but if they find more consistency, they'll have a chance to finish the season on a high note. So how will the Sooners perform in "The Swamp?" Our staff here at Sooners Wire picked this week's showdown between the Sooners and the Gators. There's also the question of how Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer will play without Ben Arbuckle on the sideline for the first time in years. picks.blurb: Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff MNF: Bills-Vikings live updates Week 10 Waiver Wire Jaguars' blockbuster deal Giannis left 'speechless' CFP doubling in size Staff Picks: Will Oklahoma Get Back on Track at No. 24 Florida? Oklahoma Sooners tight ends coach Jason Witten will take over as interim offensive coordinator for the rest of the season. | Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Chapman · Oklahoma Sooners On SI Fri, November 6, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Gators have an impressive resume, having beaten No. 4 Ole Miss 52-28 at The Swamp, then going on the road to Austin and taking down No. 7 Texas 27-24 - one week after OU beat them in Dallas - on a night the underwhelming Florida defense overwhelmed Arch Manning and the Longhorns, sacking him five times, limiting UT to 2-of-10 on third down (they had 13 first downs total) and holding the Horns to 272 total yards. But they were also blown out in back-to-back losses to No. 25 Missouri and unranked South Carolina, which preceded last week's 27-8 loss to No. 3 Georgia. Oklahoma is a touchdown underdog to Florida, but the Sooners are the best defense the Gators face. Still, OU may be reeling after its worst defensive performance in years in the blowout loss to South Carolina - which included an incomprehensible 25 missed tackles (usually 10 is a bad number). OU's first trip to The Swamp will be punctuated by another big game from Gators RB Jaden Baugh, who's third in the SEC at 100.3 rushing yards per game and first with 13 rushing TDs. Final score: Florida 28, Oklahoma 21 Things could get gross Saturday night. Florida has officially made a quarterback change, and Tramell Jones Jr. could be without a pair of key weapons to pair with an already banged up offensive line. Oklahoma's offense has been so bad it got its coordinator fired, but Jason Witten has never called plays collegiately and John Mateer is still likely the quarterback the Sooners will roll with. OU's defense needs to bounce back after its tackling struggles last week, but even an improved showing could see Gator running back Jaden Baugh have enough success to push Jon Sumrall's team across the finish line. Final: Florida 16, Oklahoma 13 OU is set up for further disaster as it heads to the swamp. Jason Witten will serve as the Sooners' play caller for the first time at the college level, John Mateer is still the quarterback and Ben Hill Griffin Stadium is one of the nation's most hostile atmospheres. But amid the weirdness, I expect OU to win this game. Teams often come out more inspired after a notable firing, and I predict Witten will lead a creative game plan as he auditions for the full-time offensive coordinator role. Florida's offense is good - but it is also prone to turning the ball over. If the Sooners are able to put pressure on Tramell Jones Jr. early, it will create a long day for the Gators' offense. Final: Oklahoma 24, Florida 20 The Sooners figure to get a little boost from Jason Witten's playcalling, but don't expect massive changes in either scheme or production here. The offensive line still has its issues, John Mateer hasn't been consistent at all, and neither of the other quarterbacks have experience in games like this. But Oklahoma's defense does figure to have a bounce-back game after struggling to contain LaNorris Sellers and the South Carolina offense. The tackling will be better, and Florida's offense is in a bit of flux itself with Tramell Jones Jr. expected to make his second start of the season at quarterback and Florida's offensive line struggling in recent weeks. But the Gators still have plenty of talent, especially on the offensive side, and The Swamp is one of the toughest environments in college football. That's a tough position for a reeling team to be placed in. The game will be close into the second half but the Gators figure to pull away and hand Oklahoma its second consecutive defeat. Final: Florida 24, Oklahoma 14 Brady Trantham A new offensive coordinator doesn'tchange the fact that John Mateer is still QB1 at OU. Mateer gives Oklahoma their best shot in any game, but in 20 games as the Sooner signal caller, it is apparent that he simply isn't very good. A coaching change can, in theory, help him in spots, but if OU needs their QB to make a play in a tight game, chances are he will make that play - just for the other team. Florida sticks to the run and gets Oklahoma on a few explosives and rides it to an easy win. Final: Florida 27, Oklahoma 16 Today's best reads Which Under the Radar Sooners Could Help Pull an Upset Over the Gators? Pete Fiutak · College Football News Sat, November 7, 2026 at 2:18 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads When we last saw Oklahoma and Florida play, the Sooners rolled 55-20 in the 2020 Cotton Bowl over a high-powered Gator team that lost to eventual national champion Alabama in an epic SEC Championship. The other meeting was the BCS Championship at the end of the 2009 season, when Tim Tebow and the Gator defense took down Heisman-winner Sam Bradford and the amazing Sooner attack 24-14 for the national title. The stakes aren't as high this time around, but for a Florida program that's on the rise, and No. 24 in the first College Football Playoff rankings, and for a 4-4 Oklahoma desperate to close strong, this will be intense. Oklahoma vs Florida: Quick Hits Oklahoma at 4-4, needs to win two of its last four to be bowl eligible. It hosts Ole Miss and Texas A&M after this before closing at Missouri. Florida is coming off the 27-8 loss to Georgia. It goes to Kentucky next, hosts Vanderbilt, and finishes at Florida State. Again, the first two meetings were in big bowl games. This is the first regular season matchup between the two. How To Watch Oklahoma vs Florida Date: Saturday, November 7, 2026 Game Time: 7:45 PM ET TV: SEC Network Location: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville, FL – Week 10 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Top 25 | Bowl Projections – Expert Picks: Week 10 Why Oklahoma Will Win The defense continues to fight the good fight. It had a problem in the 42-25 loss to South Carolina, but the defense is fantastic on third downs thanks to a pass rush that takes over games. But to beat Florida, you have to slow down the run. The Gators are 0-3 when running for fewer than 155 yards, and the Sooners give up just 107 yards per game. Only Mississippi State and, last week, South Carolina have been able to gash the Sooners for more. Why Florida Will Win Oklahoma's offense has a hard time running the ball. With a defense as good as the Sooners have, all the O has to do is keep it moving and not screw it up. But no running game means more pressing overall, and then come the mistakes. The Sooners only average 107 yards per game on the ground, and they just can't find any room to move. The Gators have to hold up, and then pounce on an Oklahoma attack that turned it over four times against both Georgia and Kentucky, three times against New Mexico, and twice against Michigan. Oklahoma vs Florida Prediction, Betting Lines It's stupid, but if you buy into these things, going back to the last two games of last season, Oklahoma is on a ten-game run of alternating wins and losses. The Sooners beat Texas, then lost to Kentucky, beat Mississippi State, lost to South Carolina, beat … Florida? The Sooners have the defense to hold up and make Florida struggle. The Gators got by Texas a few weeks ago, but it's been a struggle, losing three of the last four. Weird trends aside, this Oklahoma team really does have a way of rallying when it absolutely has to. away.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: Four Gators are listed as out: defensive lineman Jeramiah McCloud, tight end Evan Chieca, offensive lineman Emeka Ugorji and linebacker Jaden Robinson. McCloud is out due to a suspension, according to Swamp247 , while Robinson missed his first game of the season last week against Georgia. Listed as doubtful is wide receiver Vernell Brown III, who has missed the last four games with a grade-1 PCL strain that he suffered against Ole Miss in Week 4 that was re-aggravated ahead of last week's Georgia game. "So he was not available at practice today," Jon Sumrall said on Monday . "I really don't have a really strong feeling on timeline because everything early in the week last week was trending really positively until the setback on Wednesday. It sucks. It sucks for him. He's working like hell to try to get back. He's frustrated." The two players listed as questionable are wide receiver Bailey Stockton and defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Stockton has been dealing with a nagging foot injury but still played against the Bulldogs last week, finishing with 76 yards on eight catches. Wide receiver Elijah Thomas and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are listed as doubtful, while wide receiver Jer'Michael Carter, defensive backs Peyton Bowen and Eli Bowen, tight end Rocky Beers and defensive lineman Kenny Ozowalu are listed as questionable, and offensive lineman Jake Maikkula is listed as probable. WR Bailey Stockton — questionable DL Emmanuel Oyebadejo — questionable OL Eddy Pierre-Louis — doubtful WR Jer'Michael Carter — questionable DL Kenny Ozowalu — questionable OL #69 Jake Maikkula — probable Questionable (50% chance to play) The initial SEC availability report for college football's Week 10 was released on Wednesday night; the Florida Gators have seven players listed, while the Oklahoma Sooners have a whopping 16. "Jeramiah McCloud has been suspended for this week's game against Oklahoma for conduct detrimental to the team. His status with the program will be re-evaluated after this week's contest," per a statement from a program spokesperson. Sumrall added what he called his "official VB3 statement": "He wants to play. He's doing everything he can to play. He's pissed off he can't play, and he's doing everything in his power to play. It's a real injury that we thought we were on the other side of that he had a setback last week, and it sucks. I mean, it freaking sucks for him." Oklahoma has eight players who are not expected to play on Saturday: linebacker Taylor Heim, defensive back Dakoda Fields, wide receiver Trell Harris, linebacker Cole Sullivan, tight end Trynae Washington, defensive back Jacobe Johnson, and offensive linemen Ryan Fodje and Fred Hinton. home.headline: Scouting report, prediction as Florida football hosts Oklahoma
home.blurb: Off a disappointing loss to Georgia, the Florida Gators (5-3, 3-3 SEC) return home to face Oklahoma (4-4. 2-3 SEC) at The Swamp on Saturday, November 7 (7:45 p.m., SEC Network). The 6-0, 196-pound Jones is 1-0 as a starter, leading Florida o a 27-24 upset win at Texas on October 17 when Philo was out with a shoulder injury. The Gators will be down one starter on the line as right tackle Emeka Ugorji has been ruled out for the Oklahoma game. That opens up an opportunity for 6-8, 319-pound right tackle Caden Jones, who made 10 starts for the Gators last season. Florida will face a challenge against an Oklahoma defense that ranks fifth in the SEC sacks (23) and seventh in tackles for loss (6.1). The Gators will look to get star running back Jadan Baugh back going, as the 6-1, 225-pound Baugh has failed to rush for more than 100 yards in four straight games. The return of Duke Clark, who has been out close to a month due to injury, also could help spark the run game. "We've been trusting each other a lot better than what we have in the past. I feel like in the past, everybody was playing out of sync almost in a way," Florida defensive lineman Brendan Bett said. "But these last few games, I think we kind of just locked arms and just really trusted each other to compete and execute and do our jobs at an elite level." Florida will honor Hall of Fame coach Urban Meyer during the game, inducting him into the stadium's ring of honor. Meyer was involved in the process to hire Sumrall, who is trying to get the Gators back on track after a 1-3 October that included the 27-8 loss to the Bulldogs on Halloween in Atlanta. "Not what we need to do last Saturday as a team," Sumrall said. "We got an opportunity to respond this week, excited about that. A lot of growth is needed within our football team. We're hard at working, getting it done." Here are five storylines to watch in UF's matchup with the Sooners: Can Florida football QB Tramell Jones Jr. provide a spark to the offense? Florida is turning to Jones as starting quarterback after incumbent starter Aaron Philo threw two interceptions and was benched in the first half against Georgia. Jones was able to move the offense in relief of Jones against the Bulldogs, passing for 172 yards and rushing for 17 yards and a TD. "Attribute that to a lot of poise, right, and preparation," Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said. "He knows where everybody he is. There's probably a couple we'd like back, but other than that I thought he did a good job. Got to continue to work, continue to get better." For the season, Jones has passed for 579 yards and 4 TDS while throwing 3 interceptions. He's also added 83 yards and 1 TD rushing. Can Florida football OL raise its level of play to protect Jones and get the run game back going?
